AJ Mohammad Ali and MG Mahmud Shahin, Advocates ------ For the Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioner. 
Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate ------ For the Proforma-Defendant-Respondent-Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Towhidur Rahman (Md) Mandol ------ Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioner.
Vs
Principal, Rangpur Judgment Model College and others ------ Proforma-Defendant-Respondent-Opposite-Parties.
full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This Rule, at the instance of plaintiff, directed against judgment and decree dated 19-6-2011 passed by the learned Special District Judge, 1st Court, Rangpur allowing Title Appeal No. 177 of 2007 thereby dismissing Title Suit No. 27 of 2006 on reversing those dated 24-10-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rangpur, in charge of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Rangpur.

2. Plaintiff instituted the aforesaid suit praying for decree for declaration that as per decision of governing body of Rangpur Model College, plaintiff having been appointed as vice principal of the aforesaid college is in service as Vice Principal.

3. It is the case of plaintiff, in brief, that, Rangpur Model College was established in 1995 and later on, was affiliated as a Degree College in 1998, of which plaintiff was appointed as the Lecturer of Physics at the time of establishment of the college. The governing body of the college on 8-12-2001 took a resolution to appoint plaintiff as vice-principal of the college, and consequently the appointment letter was issued on 27-12-2001 and plaintiff joined the post of vice-principal on 29-12-2001. The governing body of the college by resolution dated 17-2-2002 decided to include plaintiff in the scheme of Monthly Pay Order, 1996. The governing body vides its resolution dated 27-7-2002 decided to send relevant papers to the concerned authority to pay salary to the plaintiff as vice-principal. In the meantime plaintiff carried out various duties of the college and put his signature as the vice-principal of the college from 29-12-2001 to 30-12-2004. The plaintiff on many occasions represented the college as the vice-principal of the college. Plaintiff observed that his designation on the attendance registrar was penned through and was written as Assistant Professor from 1-10-2004 to 30-12-2004 against which, he raised objection on 4-1-2005. Defendant No.1 did not give any reply to the objection of the plaintiff. Plaintiff on 29-11-2005 filed application to the Chairman of the governing body for redress his grievances but in vain. Plaintiff on 20-12-2005 filed applications for casual leave and also on 21-12-2005 and 22-12-2005 but defendant No. 1 warned the plaintiff not to use the designation of vice-principal, against which plaintiff through his learned Advocate sent a legal notice upon the defendants on 26-12-2005 but of no effect, hence the suit.

4. The case of defendant No. 1 is that, the governing body of the college appointed plaintiff as vice-principal purely on temporary basis, subject to the subsequent appointment as per rules of the National University; the notice for appointment was published in the daily 'Juger Alo' on 25-6-2002; 8 candidates including plaintiff filed application for the post of vice-principal; step was taken to have the representative present from National University as per rule; the college inspector vide memo dated 27-7-2003 refused the appointment raising the irregularities of the previous appointment of the plaintiff as Vice Principal; the governing body vide resolution dated 11-9-2004 was compelled to cancel the previous appointment of the plaintiff as vice-principal; the matter was communicated to the plaintiff on 10-11-2004, plaintiff took it normally and used his designation as Assistant Professor on many occasions; plaintiff filed Writ Petition No. 8480 of 2005 as Assistant Professor to get his arrear salary; obtained his salary for the post of Assistant Professor; plaintiff himself prepared the bill in February, 2006 and received the same by using his designation as Assistant Professor.

5. In the suit, plaintiff examined 3 witnesses including himself on the other hand defendants examined 1 witness.

6. Learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rangpur, in charge of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Rangpur by judgment and decree dated 24-10-2007 decreed the suit. Defendant No. 1 moved before the learned District Judge, Rangpur in Other Appeal No. 177 of 2007, which was transferred to the 1st Court of Additional District Judge, Rangpur for hearing, who after hearing, allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit.

7. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate, appeared for the plaintiff-petitioner, submits that, plaintiff was appointed by the governing body of the said College as Vice Principal on 27-12-2001, he joined in the said post on 29-12-2001 and was working in such post while decision of the governing body of the college was taken on 11-9-2004 removing plaintiff from the post of vice-principal without any show cause notice which violated the principle of natural justice, learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rangpur committed no illegality in decreeing the suit which court of appeal below failed to consider. Learned Advocate further submits that plaintiff challenged the decision of the governing body making them as defendant No. 2 who did not prefer any appeal, but defendant No. 1 filed the appeal who has no locus standi, as such, the appeal ought to be dismissed as the appeal was filed by a totally incompetent person. Learned Advocate further submits that the impugned judgment and decree of the court of appeal below was passed in gross violation of the established principles of law, beyond the pleadings and assessment of evidence resulting in an error in decision occasioning failure of natural justice.

8. Mr Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate, appeared for the defendant-opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that, appointment of plaintiff as vice-principal, being on temporary basis, deserved no show cause notice prior to his removal from the post of vice-principal and reverted to substantive post of the plaintiff as Assistant. Professor which, having not been affected, the plaintiff in any manner, which the learned Judge of the appellate court found and dismissed the suit in allowing the appeal and, as such, judgment having passed on consideration of materials on record, including plaint; written statement, exhibits and depositions of the witnesses, call's for no interference.

9. On consideration of the plaint and written statement, the fact related for disposal of the Rule are that plaintiff joined temporarily in the post of Lecturer for Physics on 6-9-1995, the governing body appointed plaintiff as vice-principal on 8-12-2001 and issued appointment letter on 27-12-2001, plaintiff joined as vice-principal on 29-12-2001, the governing body approved the appointment on 17-12-2002 and from 29-12-2001 to 30-12-2004 plaintiff signed as vice-principal in the daily attendance registrar. Plaintiff noticed in the daily attendance registrar of January, 2005 that his designation as vice-principal was penned, he protested but Principal remained unmoved; on 21-12-2005 Principal asked the plaintiff not to use the designation of vice-principal, hence the suit for declaration that the decision of governing body terminating his service dated 11-9-2004 is illegal and not binding upon him.

10. Defendant's facts, as put forward, are that, plaintiff was appointed as vice-principal on temporary basis and accordingly he joined on 29-12-2001; on 25-6-2002 College advertised for appointing vice-principal and plaintiff and 8 others applied on 29-9-2002 College, asked National University to send representative. But National University declined by letter dated 27-7-2003 due to irregularities in the appointment. On 13-7-2003, the governing body decided to appoint vice-principal as per rule. Plaintiff applied for promotion as Assistant Professor from the post of Lecturer on 18-7-2004, plaintiff's temporary appointment was cancelled by the governing body on 11-9-2004. Plaintiff filed Writ Petition No. 8480 of 2005 stating his designation as Assistant Professor of the college.

11. On the aforesaid factum of the instant case, question calls for determination is whether provision of natural justice has been violated in removing the plaintiff from the post of vice-principal by not issuing any show cause notice to the plaintiff.

12. To decide the question, let us refer to the appointment letter of the plaintiff as vice-principal. Plaintiff was appointed as vice principal of the college by memo dated 27-12-2001, although it appears that his appointment was temporary, but with certain conditions. The conditions are as follows:-

“১। সরকারী বেতন স্কেলে তিনি সরকার ঘোষিত তারিখ হতে বেতন প্রাপ্ত হবেন ৷

২ ৷ দক্ষতার প্রমান সাপেক্ষে তিনি ঢাকুরীতে স্থায়ত্ব লাভ করতে পারবেন।

৩ ৷ বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়, শিক্ষাবোর্ড, মন্ত্রনালয় ও কলেজ কর্তৃক জারিকৃত সকল আদেশ নিষেধ তাকে যথাযথভাবে মেনে চলতে হবে ।

8 । কমপক্ষে ৫(পাঁচ) বৎসরের পূর্বে তিনি চাকুরি হতে ইস্তফা দিতে পারবেন না ।

৫। কলেজের স্বার্থের পরিপন্থি কোন কার্য তার বিরুদ্ধ কার্য বলে বিবেচিত হবে এবং কলেজ কর্তৃপক্ষ আইনানুগ ব্যবস্থা গ্রহন করতে পারবেন ৷”

13. Condition No. 4 shows that appointment is temporary, but such temporary basis is for 5 years from his date of appointment as vice-principal as he cannot resign from his post, that means, his service is from 27-12-2001 to 27-12-2006. It gives burden upon the governing body that if plaintiff be removed before this 5 years period, he is entitled, at least for a show cause notice and also there must be an enquiry to find whether he performed his service/duty satisfactorily. If he performed his service satisfactorily then he has legitimate expectation for being appointed on permanent basis as vice-principal. If this has not been done then the principal of natural justice has been violated.

<u>14. Natural justice has no definition but is inferred from the circumstances offending morality as violation of natural justice. Natural justice is founded in equity, in honestly and right i.e. before guillotining a person whether such person was given all opportunity to defend his case. The act must not be capricious, arbitrary, mala fide and unlawful. It may be mentioned that the rules of natural justice vary with varying constitutions of statutory bodies, and the rules, prescribed by the Legislature under which they have to function, and the question whether in a particular case they have been contravened must be judged not by any preconceived notion but in the light of the provisions of the relevant Act. The expression "Natural justice" may not be capable of precise definition. But the basic and fundamental requirements of "natural justice" are well known and have been repeatedly affirmed by courts of highest authority. Particular forms of legal procedure may not be necessary, but it is of the very essence of an enquiry and a decision that the person enquiring must be one without bias and should render the decision in a judicial spirit and in accordance with the principles of substantial justice.</u>

15. In the case of Jamuna Oil Company Ltd. vs Sk Dey & another, 44 (AD) DLR 104 it is held that "Natural justice in a case of disciplinary proceeding against employee, in the absence of statutory rules, the employee must be given prior notice of the employee of the proceeding so that he gets an adequate opportunity to defend himself. In the case of Bangladesh vs Commercial Trust of Bangladesh Ltd. 46 DLR (AD) 89 it is held that "The contention that the respondent was given during on-the-spot enquiry by the Deputy Land. Reforms Commissioner will not be a sufficient compliance of the principle of natural justice, because the impugned order of derequisition was passed not by the Deputy land Commissioner but by the Ministry." In the case of Mahinuddin vs Dhaka University 45 DLR 292 it is held that "The maxim Audi Alteram Pattern; no man shall be condemned unheard, applies to judicial as well as administrative bodies, specially where the proceedings taken may affect the person or property or other rights of the parties concerned in the dispute." In the case of Professor Golam Azam vs Bangladesh, 45 DLR 423 it is held that "Natural justice is nothing but a procedural justice; being procedural it cannot be said it is not vested. In one of those situation where Natural justice clause is invoked there existed any legal right for such an asking but the matter involves what the Court often calls a legitimate expectation of procedural justice. When that is not specifically ousted by the law itself, the Court would read into the law such a clause." In the case of Ehsanul Hoque vs General Manager, Agrani Bank, 42 DLR 60 it is held that "In a case where there are no rules and regulations for conducting enquiry, the principle of natural justice is to be followed." In the case of Bangladesh vs Professor Golam Azam, 46 DLR (AD) 192 it is held that "A person who is deemed to be a citizen of Bangladesh under Article 2 is not required to take any oath of allegation unless he is elected or appointed to any office mentioned in the Third Schedule of the Constitution." In the case of Bangladesh Steamer Agents Association vs Bangladesh and others, 33 DLR (AD) 177 it is held that "it is inconceivable that when a citizen is deprived of a right vested in the person, he can be deprived of that right by a capricious or arbitrary executive fiat without being challenged as being violative of the principles of natural justice. All that this decision appears to have decided is that before a right of individual is terminated he must be heard." In the case of Abul Hossain Akand (Md) vs Abul Kalam Azad, 49 DLR 257 it is held that "The principle that no man should be condemned unheard is applicable to judicial as well as administrative bodies." In the case of Rafiqul Alam vs Secretary Ministry of Works, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, 49 DLR 456 it is held that "The principle of natural justice ought to have been complied with. Because principle of natural justice is also applicable in administrative matters as natural justice he should know the allegations against him and, as such, he should be given an opportunity of explaining his position in the matter." In the case of Principal, Chittagong Medical College vs Shahrayar Murshed, 48 DLR (AD) 33 it is held that "Fair compliance of the rule of natural justice-the first requirement of the rule is that the person to be proceeded against must be made aware of the allegations against him the right to have notice of the charges." In the case of Shahrayar Murshed vs Chittagong Medical College, 48 DLR 482 it is held that "In order to ensure the elementary and essential principles of fairness "as a matter of necessary implication the person sought to be affected must at least be made aware of the nature of the allegations against him, he should be given a fair opportunity to made any relevant statement putting forward his own case" and the authority is to give an opportunity to the person sought to be affected to correct or contradict any relevant statement prejudice to him. In order to act justly and to reach just ends by just means the Courts insist that the person or authority should have adopted the "elementary and essential principles" unless the same had been expressly excluded by the enactment empowering him to so act." In the case of Chairman, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Jessore vs Md Amir Hossain, 56 DLR (AD) 24 it is held that "Even where provision for show cause notice and opportunity of personal hearing are not available, the principle of natural justice shall be applied unless it is specifically barred."

16. The principles of natural justice are those rules which have been laid down by the courts as being the minimum protection of the rights of the individual against the arbitrary procedure that may be adopted by a judicial or quasi-judicial authority while making an order affecting those rights. These rules are intended to prevent such authority from doing injustice. These principles are four in number:-

(1) that every person whose civil rights are affected must have a reasonable notice of the case he has to meet.

(2) that he must have reasonable opportunity of being heard in his defence.

(3) that the hearing must be by an impartial tribunal, i.e. a person who is neither directly nor indirectly a party to the case or is already biased against the party concerned.

(4) that the authority must act in good faith, and not arbitrarily but reasonably.

17. It is seen that temporary appointment was given, as per clause 4 of the appointment letter for 5 years from 27-12-2001 to 27-12-2006 but it is seen that Principal of the College, defendant No. 1 on 1-10-2004 requested him not to use his disquisition as vice-principal which being made within the 5 years period, plaintiff is entitled for a show cause notice as the plaintiff was at that moment of legitimate expectation of being appointed permanently. Legitimate expectation means which shall be protected must be 'legitimate'. It may not be out of place to refer the case of Md Idrisur Rahman vs Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs 29 BLD 32 = 61 DLR 523, affirmed by the Appellate Division that the Justices who were appointed for 2 years, and having in know of such term, after expiry of 2 years period, when they were not confirmed, they were appointed on the ground of Legitimate expectation. This case is on better footing as the plaintiff was removed before the term of his initial appointment is over.

18. We have seen that appeal was preferred by incompetent person as the plaintiff challenged the decision of the governing body of the college, defendant No. 2, but appeal was preferred by the principal of the college shows that principal taken special interest over matter which expressed his bloodthirstiness against the plaintiff exposes his bias, mala fide and killing instant.

19. From the aforesaid factum of the case we are satisfied that provision of natural justice having been violated in the name of Government by the principal of the college, judgment passed by the learned Special District Judge, 1st Court, Rangpur, in Title Appeal No. 177 of 2007 was passed illegally.

20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any Order as to costs.

21. The judgment and decree dated 19-6-2011 passed by the learned Special District Judge, 1st Court, Rangpur allowing Title Appeal No. 177 of 2007 thereby dismissing Title Suit No. 27 of 2006 on reversing those dated 24-10-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rangpur, in charge of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Rangpur is set-aside. Other Suit No. 27 of 2006 is decreed.

Send down the lower court records.

Communicate this order at once.

End.

parties:
Hasan Sikder ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Jahurul Haque Molla and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam, J: This Rule arises out of the following circumstances:-The opposite party no. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 124 of 1974 in the First Court of Assistant Judge Khulna against Abdul Latif Kazi as defendant no.1 for specific performance of contract in respect of landed property measuring 1.87 acres on the basis of an alleged bainapatra dated 9.10.71 which was executed by the said Abdul Latif Kazi. During pendency of the said suit Abdul Latif Kazi died and his heirs were substituted. They found that the claim of the opposite 'party was genuine and as such they settled the matter on compromise and the suit was ultimately decreed on compromise. But after the passing of the compromise decree the heirs of late Abdul Latif Kazi i.e. defendant nos. 2-9 of the aforesaid suit changed their mind and did not voluntarily register the necessary sale deed. Finding no other alternative the opposite party no. 1 had to file Title Execution Case No. 32 of 1977 in the Court of First Munsif, Khulna and the said sale deed was registered through the Court and he took possession of the suit property through court.

2. After lapse of more than 2 years from the date of compromise decree of the aforesaid title suit the present petitioner filed "Title Suit No. 24 of 1979 in the Court of First Assistant Judge, Khulna for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 124 of the 1974 of the First Court of Munsif, Khulna is fraudulent, collusive, illegal ultra-vires, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff.

3. After filing the aforesaid suit, the petitioner who is a powerful man threatened the opposite party no. 1 to disposes him from the suit land forcibly. The opposite party no. 1 having no other alternative to defend his possession instituted Title Suit No. 159 of 1984 against the present petitioner in the Court of 3rd Assistant Judge, Khulna for permanent injunction. The present petitioner as defendant contested that suit but ultimately that suit was decreed in favour of the opposite party no. 1.

4. It appears frond the record that after filing of the said Title Suit No. 24 of 1979, by the present petitioner at no stage he did take any steps to get the bainapatra dated 9.10.71 examined by the Finger print expert. 'It is only when the suit reached its peremptory hearing stage, the plaintiff petitioner came up with an application to examine the of late Kazi Abdul Latif appearing in the bainapatra dated 9.10.71 by Finger print expert. The learned Assistant Judge vide his order dated 15.9.87 rejected the petition holding that in the suit the genuinity or otherwise of the bainapatra dated 9.10.71 is not an. issue and it is not within the scope of the suit to advert to that point in the instant suit. In the instant suit the court will adjudicate only one point that is whether the decree was Obtained fraudulently and collusively in the aforesaid. Title Suit No. 124 of 1974 and as such he rejected the prayer, of the plaintiff petitioner.

5. Mr. Sayed Golam Mustafa, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner submits that from a perusal of the plaint of Title Suit No. 24 of 1979 it appears that the plaintiff challenged the genuinity of the bainapatra dated 9.10.71 and as such it is necessary to determine the genuinity  or otherwise of the bainapatra dated 9.10.71 in the suit.

6. Mr. Abdul Jabbar, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant opposite party submits that the genuinity of the bainapatra dated 9.10.71 is not at all necessary for determining the point in issue in the instant suit. The plaintiff petitioner with ill motive of delaying the matter further and to delay the holding of the trial of the instant suit has filed this application on 15.9.87 on the date of peremptory hearing.

<u>7. On a perusal of the impugned order it is found that the learned Munsif rejected the prayer of the plaintiff petitioner on the ground that the genuineness or otherwise of the bainapatra dated 9.10.71 is not an issue and it is not necessary to determine the same in disposing the Title Suit No. 24 of 1979. It is crystal clear from the material and evidence on record that in the instant suit it is beyond the scope of the trial court to deal with the genuineness or otherwise of the bainapatra dated 9.10.71 and as such the learned Munsif rightly rejected the prayer of the plaintiff petitioner. The learned Munsif did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned order and it cannot be assailed on any ground whatsoever. There is no substance in this application which must be rejected.</u>

8. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

9.  Since Title Suit No. 24 of 1979 is pending for long time the trial court is directed to dispose of the suit as early as possible preferably within 6 months from the date of receipt of this order.

End.

full_judgment:
Quazi Reza-ul-Hoque J: The instant Rule was issued on 24-10-2013 calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo dated 9-10-2013 (annexure-H) shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, and why they shall not be directed to promote the petitioner to the post of Chief Engineer (PWD) on the basis of seniority and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. And pending hearing of the Rule, there was an order of injunction from promoting any junior of the petitioner in the post of Chief Engineer (PWD) for a period of 6(six) months.

2. The facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, as has been stated by the petitioner, in short, is that the petitioner was appointed by the respondent No. 1, as an Assistant Engineer of Public Works Department (PWD) and, accordingly, the petitioner joined the said post on 9-3-1979, and in course of his service he has been promoted to different posts from time to time (Annexure-A). The respondent No. 1 by the Notification being No. GriGoMo/Sha-1/5A-2/2009/131 dated 3-11-2010 promoted, amongst others, the petitioner from the post of Superintending Engineer to the Additional Chief Engineer (Civil) (Annexure-B).

3. The post of Chief Engineer under PWD has been vacant since 17-8-2011 and hence, it was bonafide and legitimate expectation of the petitioner, who is one of the senior Additional Chief Engineers of PWD, that he will be promoted to the post of Chief Engineer under PWD. And to the utter surprise of all and notwithstanding that there were other senior eligible candidates available for consideration of promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD, the respondent No. 1 by the Notification being No. GriGoMo/Sha-I/5A-3/2009/91 dated 17-8-2011 assigned the additional charge to one personnel, namely, Md. Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, to perform the current functions of Chief Engineer under PWD. Subsequently, the respondent No. 1 by the Notification being No. GriGoMo /Sha-1/4P-1 /2011/104 dated 22-9-2011 posted the aforesaid personnel, namely, Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan (the said Current Charge holder) in the post of Chief Engineer (Current Charge) of PWD (Annexures-C and C-1).

4. The respondent No. 1 had earlier by the Notification being No. 25.013.2012.05.003.2010-69 dated 30-6-2011 promoted, amongst others, the said Current Charge holder to the post of Additional Chief Engineer (Civil) from the post of superintending Engineer, whilst the petitioner is senior to the said Current Charge-holder and enlisted at Serial No. 128 of the Gradation List of PWD, while the said Current Charge-holder is enlisted at Serial No. 133 of the Gradation List (Annexures-D and D-1).

5. The respondent No. 1 by the Notification 18-10-2012 posted the said Current Charge-holder as Director (Current Charge) of Housing and Building Research Institute, Dams Salam, Mirpur, Dhaka, thus removing him from the post of Chief Engineer (current Charge) under PWD and, simultaneously, another personnel, namely, Khondokar Salahuddin and enlisted at serial No. 127 of the gradation list of PWD (who is senior to the said Current Charge-holder), was assigned the post of Chief Engineer (Current Charge) under PWD. Subsequently, the respondent No. 1 by the Notification being No. 25.013.011.05.00.003.2009-09 dated 28-1-2013 again posted the said current Charge-holder as Chief Engineer (Current Charge) of PWD (Annexures-E and E-1).

6. In order to consider proposal for promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD, the respondent No. 1 by the Memo being No. 25.00.0000.013.12.003.09-533 dated 13-8-2013 made an enquiry before the Anti-Corruption Commission, Head Office, Dhaka to provide information as to whether there were any corruption-related allegations or cases against the top 7(seven) officials of PWD which included the petitioner and the said current Charge-holder at Serial Nos. 3 and 7 respectively (Annexure- F); and in reply to the aforesaid Memo dated 13-8-2013 issued by respondent No. 1 the Anti-Corruption Commission, Head Office, Dhaka by Memo being No. DuDoK/ProSha: O LoGi: /35/2007 (Ongsho-3)/26006 dated 18-9-2013 stated that there were no allegation, inquiry, investigation or case pending against the said top 7 (seven) officials of PWD (Annexure-G).

7. In the meantime, the respondent No. 1 by the impugned Memo being No. 25.00.0000.013.12.001.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 submitted a summary for Superior Selection Board (SSB) for promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD. It is evident from the said Memo dated 9-10-2013 that only the name of the said Current Charge-holder was proposed to the SSB for promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD, although there were 6(six) personnel (including the petitioner) who were eligible for promotion, who are senior to the said Current Charge-holder (Annexure-H).

8. At all relevant times, the top 7 (seven) officials of PWD including the petitioner were under consideration for promotion for the post of Chief Engineer. In this regard, a circular dated 2-9-1991 issued by the then Ministry of Establishment is relevant, which categorically provides, inter alia, that a minimum number of 5(five) personnel should be proposed to the SSB for promotion for each vacant post. In compliance, with the aforesaid Circular dated 2-9-1991 the respondent No. 1 issued a Memo being No. 25.018.005.02.00.002.2013-323 dated 5-8-2013 stating, amongst others, that there are no allegations of any misconduct or any pending cases against the petitioner. It is further stated that the Ministry of Public Administration vide letter No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 had asked the respondent No. 1 to send a proper proposal for promotion in compliance with the circular dated 2-9-1991 along with approved gradation list and the organogram categorically stating, inter alia that there was substantial discrepancies and mistakes in the earlier proposal dated 9-10-2013 (Annexures I, I-1 and 1-2).

9. The respondent No. 5 by the Memo being No. 05.133.006.05.01.01.2013-244 dated 9-10-2013 issued a notice for the 11th (Eleventh) Meeting of SSB for the year 2013 to be held on 20-10-2013. It is pertinent to note here that promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD was not included as an agenda in the said meeting. However, the petitioner learnt from a reliable source that the promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD was also taken up for consideration in the said meeting of SSB held on 20-10-2013, although it was not initially made an agenda for the said meeting. From the aforesaid actions of the respondents, it is evident that the respondents at the behest of a vested quarter are bent upon in promoting a particular individual, namely, the said Current Charge-holder, as Chief Engineer of PWD inspite of the fact that the said Current Charge-holder is enlisted at Serial No. 133 in the Gradation List and thus there are 6(six) other personnel, including the petitioner who is enlisted at Serial No. 128 of the Gradation List, who are senior to the said Current Charge-holder (Annexure- J).

10. It is stated that as per the seniority list of Additional Chief Engineer of PWD, the petitioner is at Serial No. 3 against the said Current Charge-holder's Serial No. 7, who is now holding the post of Chief Engineer on Current Charge.

11. Serial No. 1, Column No. 4 of Part XII of the Bangladesh Civil Service recruitment Rules, 1981 ("the Rules 1981") provides that the vacant post of Chief Engineer under PWD shall be filled by way of promotion from amongst the Additional Chief Engineers having a total service experience of 18 (Eighteen) years including 3 (three) years’ experience as Additional Chief Engineer and in the meantime, the petitioner has completed about 34 (thirty four) years of service with an unblemished record. It is pertinent to note here that the petitioner has already completed more than 2(two) years and 11 (eleven) months in his service as Additional Chief Engineer, while the said Current Charge-holder has only completed, only about 02(two) years and 3(three) months in his service as Additional Chief Engineer (Annexure-K).

12. It is stated that as per Circular dated 5-2-1992, issued by the then Ministry of Establishment, the order of Current Charge shall be made on the basis of seniority/gradation list and accordingly, the assigning of the said Current Charge-holder with the post of Chief Engineer (Current Charge) under PWD is not tenable in law.

13. The respondent No. 1 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition and contended inter alia that the post of Chief Engineer has been vacant since 17-8-2011. Government considering all the factors for promotion, Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, Additional Chief Engineer has been given the charge as Chief Engineer in the Current Charge vide Memo No. GriGoMo/Sha-1/SA-3/2009/91 dated 17-8-2011 & Memo No. GriGoMo/Sha-1/4P-1/2011/104 dated 22-9-11. The petitioner is not the senior most among the Additional Chief Engineers. Chief Engineer post is the post of head of the Department and policy making Government, so considering the previous service records & performance of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan is entrusted with the responsibility of Chief Engineer for the betterment of the Department. In BCS Public Works, recruitment Rules, the criteria of promotion for the cost of Chief Engineer is to have 18 years service with at least 3 years as Additional Chief Engineer in the feeder post on the basis of seniority.

14. The Government considering all facts found Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan as the finest candidate amongst the Additional Chief Engineers and thus has given him the current charge of Chief Engineer, who has been promoted to the rank of Additional Chief Engineer on 25013.012.05.003.2010-69 dated 30-6-201.

15. The Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide Memo No.25.00.0000.013.12.001.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 send proposal to the Superior Service Selection Board (SSB) proposing the name of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, considering the services rendered by him for last 2 years. He is running the department very efficiently and made expansion of the department by creating huge number of posts in different level. Considering the previous service career, he is doing better for the department in the given current charge for the post of Chief Engineer, while other addition Chief Engineers are working, under him for more than two years. On considering his performance for running the PWD smoothly and efficiently for 2 years, the Ministry has proposed his name to the SSB. BCS Public Works Recruitment Rule, criteria for promotion to Chief Engineer is "Amongst the Additional Chief Engineer" with 18 years' with 3 years' service in the feeder post. For promotion to the top post only seniority is not the basis of promotion. Government should consider the capability, efficiency and his previous service-records; even in the past seniority have never been the criteria for pro-motion to the post of Chief Engineer.

16. The Circular dated 2-9-1991, Ministry of Establishment prescribed minimum number of 5 (five) personnel to be proposed vide Memo No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013, and asked to send more name in accordance with circular 2-9-1991. Accordingly Ministry of Housing and Public Works send proposal of 7(seven) names including the name of the petitioner to the SSB vide Memo No. 25.00.0000.013.012.005.09.700 dated 20-10-2013. Here the petitioner suppressed the fact that only one name has been send to SSB, in fact 7(seven) names including the name of petitioner has been send in the SSB.

17. The responded No. 5 issued notice vide Memo No. 05.133.006.05.01.01.2013.244 dated 9-10-2013 for 11 (eleventh) meeting of SSB for the year 2013 to be held on 20-10-2013 and vide Memo No. 25.00.0000.013.12.01.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 a proposal has been sent to SSB, Ministry of Public Administration vide letter No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 asked the respondent No. 1 to send a proposal in accordance with a circular date 2-9-1991.

18. The Government considering Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, fit for the post of Chief Engineer, for the betterment of the department, as the respondent No. 6, at present is in the current charge at the post of Chief Engineer and he is running the department in a very well manner, and since he has served in the post for last 2 years while all other Additional Chief Engineers are working under him.

19. The petitioner all the time suppressed the fact and mentioned that only one name is proposed for meeting, in fact respondent No. 1, vide proposal dated on 20-10-13 sent fresh proposal with 7(seven) names, which included the name of the petitioner.

20. The respondent No. 2 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition, and stated inter alia that the Ministry of Housing and Public Works as the Administrative Ministry forwarded a proposal dated 9-10-2013 in the form of summary for promotion containing only one name that of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuyian Additional Chief Engineer. But the set Rule regarding submission of proposal for promotion to be placed before the Superior Selection Board (SSB) directs to send at least 5 names and other necessary particulars against 1 post. Subsequently, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide their letter dated 20-10-2013 submitted a revised proposal containing 7 names and particulars of possible candidates for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, PWD. Since the proposal dated 9-10-2013 was not acted upon, therefore the writ petition is liable to be discharged.

21. On 20-10-2013, SSB discussed the matter of promotion to the post of Chief Engineer of PWD on the basis of agenda No. 16 (Miscellaneous) of the said notice. A total of 7(seven) persons were proposed for consideration for the promotion of 1 position. According to the proposal of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan had been found eligible by SSB for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, PWD, since 5 others including the petitioner hand shortcomings in ACR and 1 other was working on deputation in RAJUK. In addition, the members of the SSB were of opinion that more information was required regarding the satisfactory service record of those 6 officers. And Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, Additional Chief Engineer, PWD was recommended for promotion to the Post of Chief Engineer, PWD subject to condonation of service length by the President of the Republic.

22. Although the petitioner is at serial number 3 in the seniority list while Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, is at serial No. 7 but all other 6 candidates including the petitioner hand shortcoming in the Annual Confidential Report (ACR), which is very crucial for taking decision regarding such promotion cases. The post of Chief Engineer, PWD fell vacant on 11-8-2010 and this department involves many important public works for which Md Kabir Ahmed was assigned with the Additional Charge as the Chief Engineer, PWD. It is a fact that Bangladesh Civil Service Recruitment Rules, 1981 provides that the vacant post of Chief Engineer, PWD shall be filed tip by way of promotion from amongst the Additional Chief Engineers having a total service experience of 18 years including 3 years’ experience as Additional Chief Engineer. Md Kabir Ahmed did not fulfil the requirement of 3 years’ experience as Additional Chief Engineer for which the SSB left the issue of service length condonation under the good conscience of the President.

23. Seniority is not the only criteria of promotion or to place a person on current charge rather experience, reputation, competency etc. are considered while promoting and/or placing any officer at a suitable post in the Government.

24. The petitioner misconceived and misled the actual fact. The fact remains that the Ministry of Housing and Public Works as the Administrative Ministry forwarded a proposal dated 9-10-2013 in the form of summary for promotion containing only one name and particulars that of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, Additional Chief Engineer. But the set Rule regarding submission of proposal for promotion to be placed before the Superior Selection Board (SSB) is to send at least 5 names against 1 post, unless otherwise. Subsequently the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide their letter dated 20-10-2013 submitted a revised proposal containing 7 names and particulars of possible candidates for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, PWD.

25. The petitioner claimed seniority as the basis of promotion, in fact, seniority is not the only basis of promotion or to place a person on current charge, rather experience, reputation, competency, etc. are considered while promoting and/or placing any officer at a suitable post.

26. The respondent No. 6 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending that the petitioner is an Additional Chief Engineer of the Department of Public Works and he being a Government Employee cannot file this writ petition raising disputes regarding his promotion, which clearly falls within the terms and condition of service, as such, the Rule is not maintainable and hence the Rule is liable to be discharged.

27. Seniority is not the only basis for which the petitioner can claim legitimate expectation to be promoted to the post of Chief Engineer of PWD.

28. The post of Chief Engineer has been vacant since 17-8-2011. The respondent No. 1 considering the efficiency, competency and previous brilliant service record of respondent No. 6, is bestowed with charge of Chief Engineer (current charge) vide memo No- Gri GoMo/Sha-1/ SA-3/2009/91 dated 17-8-2011 & Memo No- GriGoMo/Sha-1/4p-1/2011/104 dated 22-9-11.

29. The respondent No. 6 was transferred as Director (Current Charge) of Housing and Building Research Institute, Darusalam, Mirpur; Khandaker Salauddin (Gradation No. 127) was posted as Chief Engineer (Current Charge) superseding his senior Fazlul Kader (Gradation No. 112) and subsequently the respondent No.1 vide notification No. 25.013.011.05.00.003.2009-09 dated 28-1-2013, again posted the respondent No. 6 as Chief Engineer (Current Charge).

30. The respondent No. 1, Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide memo No. 25.00.0000.013.12.001.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 considering the services rendered by respondent No. 6 in last 2 years as Chief Engineer (Current Charge) and fulfilling other criterion for promotion sent summary to the SSB proposing the name of the respondent No. 6 for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer. Thereafter the respondent No. 2 vide memo No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 asked the respondent No. 1 to send fresh proposal fulfilling the conditions as stated in office order as contained in Memo being No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 issued by respondent No. 2. In compliance with the said Memo dated 10-10-2013 respondent No. 1 sent a fresh proposal containing 7(seven) names including the name of the petitioner and respondent No. 6 and all other information as sought for vide letter as contained in SSB memo No. 25.00.0000.013.012.005.09.700 dated 20-10-2013.

31. The respondent No. 5 circulated a notice on 9-10-2013 of 11th meetings of the SSB to be held on 20-10-2013. The respondent No. 1 on 9-10-2013 sent a summary for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer. On receipt of the summary the respondent No. 2 asked the respondent No. 1 to send fresh proposal following the circular of the Ministry of Public Administration dated 2-9-1991. Thereafter in compliance to the letter the respondent No. 1 on 20-10-2013 sent a fresh proposal containing seven names of Additional Chief Engineers including the name of the petitioner for consideration of the SSB to be held on 20-10-2013. Though the petitioner challenged the summary dated 9-10-2013 for not sending his name in the said summary, but on 20-10-2013 a fresh proposal has been sent including the name of the petitioner, and Rule has been issued on 24-10-2013 as such, the Rule has become infructuous and considering efficiency and previous brilliant service record of the respondent No. 6, respondent No. 1 the gave him the current charge of Chief Engineer on 17-8-2011 and he has been performing his duties efficiently and satisfactorily for last 2 years and all the Additional Chief Engineers including the petitioner are working under him without any grievance.

32. The respondent No. 6 obtained his graduation in Civil Engineering, securing 1st, Class 3rd position from the University of Chittagong in the year 1978. Thereafter he joined as. Assistant Engineer in the Department of Public Works on 10-3-1979 and subsequently he was promoted to the post of Sub Divisional Engineer in 1983. He was thereafter promoted as Executive Engineer on 22-3-2001 and Superintending Engineer on 13-9-2009. In recognition of his efficient and meritorious service he was promoted to the post of Additional Chief Engineer on 30-6-2011 (Annexures-1, 2, 3, 4 and 5).

33. Mr Salauddin Dolon with Mr Md Mohammad Shirajum Monir the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner submitted that the impugned recommendation dated 9-10-2013 is ex-facie illegal, malafide, unwarranted and without lawful authority because the same has been made in violation of the Circular 2-9-1991 and devastatingly affecting the valuable rights of the petitioner and other seniors who have the rights to be promoted ahead of their juniors, if they are not found, otherwise disqualified.

34. On point of maintainability in writ jurisdiction he submitted that Dr Nurul Islam's case, 33 DLR (AD) 201, is the first milestone case in service matter on the ground of discrimination and dissimilar treatment to the similar situated and also the rights of a Government servant and duties of the Government under Article 135 of the Constitution, wherein it is amply discussed. And the second milestone case is Mujibur Rahman vs Bangladesh, 44 DLR (AD) 111 was observed inter alia that:

.......Within its jurisdiction the Tribunal can strike down an order for violation of principles of natural justice as well as for infringement of fundamental rights, guaranteed by the Constitution, or of any other law, in respect, of matters relating to or arising of sub-clause (a), but such tribunals cannot, like the Indian Administrative Tribunals in exercise of more comprehensive jurisdiction under Article 323A  strike down any law or rule on the ground of its constitutionality. A person in the service of the Republic who intends to invoke fundamental rights for challenging the vires of a law will seek this remedy under Article 102(1), but in all other cases he will be required to seek remedy under Article 117(2).

35. The view of Mujibar Rahman case was changed in the case of Bangladesh vs Shafiuddin, 50 DLR (AD) 27, and the Appellate Division found the writ petitions maintainable by observing that:

The supplemental, as opposed to substitution, role of the Tribunal constituted under Article 117 of the Constitution was already conceded and permitted to the Tribunals in Mujibur Rahmann case and no power of judicial review under Article 102(2) was conceded to the Tribunals in that case. The writ petitioners' relief could not have been obtained by a supplemental role performed by the Tribunals. They have rightly invoked the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102(1) of the Constitution. The writ petitions were fully maintainable.

36. And in the case of Delwar Hossain Mia (Md) vs Bangladesh, 52 DLR (AD) 120 the Apex  Court again relied upon the decision of Mujibur Rahman case, observing inter alia that:

........A person in the service of the Republic who intends to invoke fundamental rights for challenging the vires of a law will seek his remedy under Article 102(1), but in all other cases he will be required to seek remedy under Article 117(2).

37. In the instant case the petitioner has sought remedy under Article 102(2), since right guaranteed and protected by the Constitution has been infringed.

38. Thereafter in the landmark case of Bangladesh vs Md Shamsul Huq, 59 DLR (AD) 54 [Bench Officer's Case], the Appellate Division found the case maintainable on the ground of 'disparity and discrimination of pay' among the similarly situated.

39. In the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Md Abdur Rashid, 12 BLC (AD) 142 exactly on the same point the Appellate Division found the case of the Government servants maintainable.

40. The case of the petitioner of this petition is fully maintainable as being covered by the decisions cited herein above. It is worth mentioning that in the cases reported in 59 DLR and 12 BLC, the Apex Courts have made a departure from their earlier decisions inasmuch as all the previous decisions have been over-ruled by implication. And relying on the latest decisions the decisions was given by observations made in 17 BLC 355, as follows:

The High Court Division can also entertain writ petition of a kind upon a view that the remedy before the Administrative Tribunal is not efficacious or that under the particular facts and circumstances of the cases the writ petition can be entertained, notwithstanding availability of alternative remedy before the Tribunal.

41. Relying on the same principle, the Appellate Division in Khalilur Rahman vs Md Kamrul Ahsan, 11 MLR (AD) 5 = 10 BLC (AD) 193, observed inter alia that:

As provided under section 4 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 Administrative Tribunals have exclusive jurisdiction to decide and determine any dispute relating to the terms and condition of service of a person in the service of the Republic or of Statutory Authorities with the ouster of the Jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 117(2) of the Constitution. Administrative Tribunals have no authority to issue any ad interim order restraining the Government or the statutory bodies. Except in cases involving the constitutionality of any law High Court Division cannot entertain any writ petition in respect of dispute relating to the terms and conditions of service.

42. In the case of M Abu Raihan vs Bangladesh, 7 BLC 44, this Court observed inter alia that:

If the eligible person is not considered for promotion, in such case the aggrieved person can enforce his right by invoking constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court Division as such right cannot be enforced by invoking jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal.

43. It means a person seeking direction for any inaction in the nature of mandamus cannot go to the Administrative Tribunal for not having an order.

44. In Mollah Md Anwarul Haque vs Government of Bangladesh, VIII ADC (Appellate Division Cases) 787, the Appellate Division had dealt with the matter of non-consideration of promotion and modified the High Court's order to the effect that:

The respondent No. 1 shall consider the case of the petitioners for promotion to the post of Joint Secretary, following the Guidelines.

45. And a similar view was taken in the case of Matiur Rahman vs Bangladesh, 50 DLR Page 357 (Relevant Paragraph 21). The instant petitioner also stands on the same footing as such his right to promotion is a clear expectation while he stands on similar substratum.

46. In Writ Petition No. 1405 of 2011, a Division Bench of this Court on 29-5-2012, directed the respondents to consider the case of the petitioners for promotion to the post of Deputy Secretary and thereafter Joint Secretary.

<u>47. According to section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act there must be an action or an order against which appeal is required to be filed and after 2 months of filing such appeal a person can file a case before the Administrative Tribunal. Therefore, no case under section 4(2) of the AT Act can be filed before, making or issuance of the final order as such the instant petition and its cause of action are not amenable to the Administrative Tribunal.</u>

48. The instant petitioner seeks remedy for flagrant violation of equal protection of law as guaranteed under Article 27 of the Constitution. He further submits that although the respondents have made an untrue and absurd statement that the Annual Confidential Report (ACR) of 6 senior officers are splashed with bad marks, while only ACR of the respondent No. 6 was found clean. The Annexure No. 8 submitted by the respondent No. 6 shows that there is no disciplinary report against any of the 7 incumbents. And even on the basis of query by the respondent No. 1 (Annexure-9), Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) also opined in the negative (Annexure-10). The ACR report sent to the SSB by the respondent No. 1 (Annexure-13), clearly shows that the aggregate of preceding 5 years was as follows:

AKM Fazlul Quader-92.75

Khandker Salahuddin- 95.60

AZM Tajul Islam- 95.75

SM Rafiqul Islam-92.66

Nasiruddin Mahmud Chowdhury- 94.25

Chitta Ranjan Das- 92.115; and

Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuyian- 93.40

49. Which very conspicuously resembles that while by attaining 92.75 marks the instant petitioner stood at first position against Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuyian, respondent No. 6, with 93.40 marks who stood at fourth position as yet, without any negative stigma and with the highest ACR points, the petitioner was deprived of the right to promotion and very discriminatorily, the name of respondent No. 6 name was included and proposed for promotion and he was given current charge of the Chief Engineer by passing 6 of his seniors.

50. He further submitted that promotion is an advancement in career and an employee joins in any service seeing the promotional opportunity in future and denial of promotion always create frustration in his mind, which is also violative of his fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 29 of the Constitution, inasmuch as, promotions are made available in every wings of service to bring efficiency in the service and to foster appropriate attitude to grow for the purpose of achieving excellence, therefore failure to make promotion of the senior like the petitioner will certainly lead to degeneration and stagnation, thereby destroying the urge of work of the others in the department, as such, the respondents may kindly be directed to make promotion in the post of Chief Engineer (PWD) on the basis of seniority.

51. He again submitted that as per decisions of our Apex Court in several cases, promotion of a junior ahead of many seniors is ex-facie, illegal and bad in law and from the sequence of the events and the conduct of the respondents it is manifestly clear that they would promote the Current Charge holder at any cost by devastatingly affecting the valuable service rights of many of the seniors including the petitioner, which may kindly be restrained to do so, as otherwise, the petitioner would suffer irreparable losses and injuries.

52. Mr Dolon, further submitted that the impugned memo dated 9-10-2013 is arbitrary, malafide, unreasonable inasmuch as the respondents at the behest of a vested quarter are bent upon in promoting a particular individual as Chief Engineer of the PWD, in spite of the fact that, the said Current Charge-holder is enlisted at Serial No. 133 in the Gradation List and thus there are 6(Six) other personnel (including the petitioner who is enlisted a Serial No. 128 of the Gradation List, who are senior to the said Current Charge-holder.

53. He further submitted that the entire process is being completed in a secretive manner and the petitioner inspite of strenuous efforts could not collect any papers except the summary of the Administrative Ministry and the valid objection raised by the Ministry of Public Administration dated 10-10-2013, inasmuch as, the respondents are very much aware about the circular of the Ministry of Public Administration dated 10-10-2013 but only to promote the Current Charge holder they were reluctant to fulfil the minimum requirement of law which has vitiated the entire process.

54. He again submitted that the general principal is that every employee has right to have his case considered for promotion according to his turn on the basis, of seniority, therefore, it is the cardinal principal in service jurisprudence to promote senior eligible candidate first, if they are not found otherwise unsuitable, inasmuch as, admittedly seniority is not the sole criterion for promotion but that does not give unbridled and unguided power to any authority to promote an officer who is at serial No. 133 in the Gradation List by excluding 6 seniors who are waiting in the zone of promotion and have the rights to be considered first ahead of the respondent No. 6.

55. He further submitted that the respondents at first sent the names of the 7 candidates including the petitioner to the ACC though the circular has obligated them to send 5 names but only to promote the current post holders 2 additional names have been sent which is good enough to attest the validity of the statements of the petitioner, inasmuch as, no reason has been assigned by the respondents about exclusion of the petitioner from the list of eligible candidates and no departmental proceeding is pending against the petitioner, therefore he has every legal right to claim his promotion and in all fairness respondents are bound to promote him at once.

56. Mr Dolon, further submitted that in service jurisprudence not only promotion but seniority is also related with advancement in career and promotion is often based on seniority and even in case of promotions made on seniority-cum-merit, seniority has the most important role to play inasmuch as the first recognised modes of promotion in only basis of seniority subject to fitness which has been recognised as "non-selection" method wherein merit has nothing to do and the seniority plays the most important role, therefore in judicial review Court has ample power to intervene to protect the petitioner from arbitrary action by the executive authorities.

57. Mr MK Rahman, the learned Additional Attorney-General, with Mr Biswojit Roy, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing for the respondent No. 1, submitted that the Ministry of Housing and Public Works as the Administrative Ministry forwarded a proposal dated 9-10-2013 in the form of summary for promotion containing only one name that of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuyian, Additional Chief Engineer. But the set Rule regarding submission of proposal for promotion to be placed before the Superior Selection Board (SSB) directs to send at least 5 names and other necessary particulars against 1 post. Subsequently, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide their letter dated 20-10-2013 submitted a revised proposal containing 7 names and particulars of possible candidates for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, PWD. Since the proposal dated 9-10-2013 was not acted upon, therefore the writ petition is liable to be discharged.

58. He further submitted that the instant Rule relates to conditions of service, as the petitioner is claiming promotion, which is amenable before the Administrative Tribunal as constituted under the provisions of Article 117 of the Constitution and in that regard our Apex Court has time and again has observed, as such, the Rule is not maintainable and liable to be discharged.

59. Mr Shafique Ahmed, the learned Senior Advocate with Mr SM Rezaul Karim, and Mr Mahabub Shafique, Advocates, appearing for the respondent No.6, submitted that the petitioner is an Additional Chief Engineer of the Department of Public Works and he being a Government Employee cannot file this writ petition raising disputes regarding the promotion, which clearly falls within the terms and condition of service, as such, the Rule is not maintainable and hence the Rule is liable to be discharged.

60. He further submitted that to invoke the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 102(1) is to challenge vires of a law, which the petitioner did not, rather he resorted to just challenging an order, as such, the instant Rule is liable to be discharged and in this regard he referred to the observations made in Mujibur Rahman vs Bangladesh, 44 DLR (AD) 111; Bangladesh vs Shafiuddin, 50 DLR(AD) 27; Delwar Hossain Mia (Md) vs Bangladesh, 52 DLR (AD) 120; and Khalilur Rahman vs Md Kamrul Ahsan, 11 MLR (AD) 5 = 10 BLC (AD) 193 (already cited above).

61. He further submitted that seniority is not the only basis for which the petitioner can claim legitimate expectation to be promoted to the post of Chief Engineer of PWD. The post of Chief Engineer has been vacant since 17-8-2011. The respondent No.1 considering the efficiency, competency and previous brilliant service record of respondent No. 6, is bestowed with charge of Chief Engineer (current charge) vide memo No. Gri GoMo/Sha-1 /SA-3 /2009 /91 dated 17-8-2011 & Memo No- Gri GoMo /Sha-1/4p-1/2011/104 date 22-9-11.

62. He further submitted that the respondent No. 6 was transferred as Director (Current Charge) of Housing and Building Research Institute, Darusalam, Mirpur; Khandaker Salauddin (Gradation No. 127) and was posted as Chief Engineer (Current Charge) superseding his senior Fazlul Kader (Gradation No. 112) and subsequently the respondent No.1 vide notification No. 25.013.011.05.00.003.2009-09 dated 28-1-2013, again posted the respondent No. 6 as Chief Engineer (Current-Charge) of the PWD.

63. Mr Ahmed, further submitted that the respondent No.1, Ministry Housing and Public Works vide memo No-25.00.0000.013.12.001.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 considering the services rendered by respondent No. 6 in last 2 years as Chief Engineer (Current-Charge) and fulfilling other criterion for promotion sent summary to the SSB proposing the name of the respondent No. 6 for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer. Thereafter the respondent No. 2 vide memo No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 asked the respondent No. 1 to send fresh proposal fulfilling the conditions as stated in office order as contained in Memo being No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 issued by respondent No.2. In compliance with the said Memo dated 10-10-2013 respondent No. 1 sent a fresh proposal containing 7(seven) names including the name of the petitioner and respondent No. 6 and all other information as sought for vide letter as contained in SSB memo No-25.00.0000.013.012.005.09.700 dated 20-10-2013.

64. He again submitted that the respondent No. 5 circulated a notice on 9-10-2013 of 11th meetings of the SSB to be held on 20-10- 2013.The respondent No. 1 on 9-10-2013 sent a summary for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer. On receipt of the summary the respondent No. 2 asked the respondent No. 1 to send fresh proposal following the circular of the Ministry of Public Administration dated 2-9-1991. Thereafter in compliance to the letter the respondent No. 1 on 20-10-2013, sent a fresh proposal containing 7 names of the Additional Chief Engineers including the name of the petitioner for consideration of the SSB to be held on 20-10-2013. Though the petitioner challenged the summary dated 9-10-2013 for not sending his name in the said summary, but on 20-10-2013 a fresh proposal has been sent including the name of the petitioner, and Rule has been issued on 24-10-2013, as such, the Rule has become infructuous and considering efficiency and previous brilliant service record of the respondent No. 6, respondent No. 1, gave him the current charge of Chief Engineer on 17-8-2011 and he has been performing his duties efficiently and satisfactorily for last 2 years and all the Additional Chief Engineers including the petitioner are working under him without any grievance.

65. He further submitted that the respondent No. 6 obtained his graduation in Civil Engineering, securing 1st Class 3rd position from the University of Chittagong in the year 1978. Thereafter he joined as Assistant Engineer in the Department of Public Works on 10-3-1979 and subsequently he was promoted to the post of Sub Divisional Engineer in 1983. He was thereafter promoted as Executive Engineer on 22-3-2001 and Superintending Engineer on 13-9-2009. In recognition of his efficient and meritorious service he was promoted to the post of Additional Chief Engineer on 30-6-2011 (Annexure-1, 2, 3, 4 and 5).

66. On perusal of the submission of both the parties, the petition, the affidavit-in-opposition and the available documents, it is quite apparent note that the authority concerned for filling up the vacancy of the Chief No. 6 for promotion to the said post as a single candidate for perusal of the Superior Service Selection Board (SSB) by Memo No. ২৫.০০.০০০০.০১৩.১২.০০১.০৯.৬৭৮ তারিখঃ ৯ অক্টোবর ২০১৩ (Annexure-H). And that memo has been sent back by the Ministry of Public Administration by order dated 10-10-2013 vide Memo No. ০৫.১৩৩.০১২.২৩৩.২৫.০২.২০১৩-২৪৪ (Annexure 1-2) thereafter vide Memo No. ২৫.০০.০০০০.০১৩.১২.০০১.০৯.৬৭৮ তারিখঃ ৯ অক্টোবর ২০১৩ (Annexure-13) names of 7(seven) Additional Chief Engineers were sent for consideration, wherein name of the respondent No. 6 was included, who at that time did not have the requisite qualification in service, i.e. 3(three) years’ experience in the feeder post. In fact none of the said 7(seven) candidates had the 3(three) years’ experience in the feeder post for which condonation from the fitness of the President of the Republic was required as per notification dated 1-1-1991 of the Establishment Division (Regulation Wing, Cabinet Secretariat). The proposal sent to the SSB on 20-10-2013, proposed the condonation for relaxation under Article-k8 of the notification dated 1-1-1991, was sought only for the respondent No. 6, while condonation ought to have been sought for all the candidates or in the alternative that condonation ought to have been kept open only for the person to whom the SSB gives recommendation for promotion, instead proposing recommendation for the same person not having fulfilled 3(three) years in the feeder post bypassing the 6(six) seniors and the concerned public authority's previous conduct of sending single name for promotion to the SSB by passing 6(six) seniors and without tabling gradation list before the SSB seriously portrays, mala fide and malicious conduct of the concerned public authority of biasness in favour of a single candidate, i.e. respondent No. 6. In such view of the matter, we are of the view that such a proposal superseding 6(six) seniors while the requirement was to send at least 5(five) names, that was done only to favour a single person, i.e. the respondent No. 6, is nothing but biasness, malicious, mala fide and colourable exercise of power, on part of the public authority. The whole process from the beginning of sending a single name thereafter on its rejection sending 7(seven) names including the name of the respondent No. 6 clearly resembles that, the concerned public authority pre-determined to promote respondent No. 6 to the post of Chief Engineer.

67. The contesting respondents have stated that the ACR of the 6 other Additional Chief Engineers, except the ACR of the respondent No. 6 was not satisfactory, but on perusal of the relevant papers, it clearly resembles that none of the ACRs had any stigma upon any of the seven, rather it is quite apparent that in the ACR markings the petitioner stood in the position with 9-2-75 marks as against the respondent No. 6, securing only 93.40 marks in serial No. 4, in terms of merit.

68. While 6 senior officers are quite ably competent, even than superseding them giving charge of Chief Engineer to the 7th person in the list of seniority, itself is a flagrant violation of natural justice forcing the said 6 seniors to serve under the junior most Additional Chief Engineer. It clearly portrays that the authority did not treat all its employees equally. In AKM Kawser Ahmed vs Bangladesh, 65 DLR 377, it was observed inter alia that:

The doctrine or legitimate expectation imposes in spirit a duty on public authority to act fairly by taking into consideration all relevant factors relating to such legitimate expectations.

69. In the instant case the concerned public authority has utterly failed to act fairly, which quite apparent from the submissions of the petitioner and, as well as, respondents, since the respondents could not show any justification with regard to proposing the name of the respondent No. 6 for promotion superseding 6 other Additional Chief Engineers, who did not at all stood in any better standing than to the petitioner, therefore the Rule deserves merit.

<u>70. On point of maintainability, it is to be noted that, if mala fide, biasness and irregularity is visible mingled with legitimate expectation, writ jurisdiction is the right place to vindicate someone's right that has been infringed.</u>

<u>In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the proposal send by the Ministry of Housing and Public Works for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer from amongst the proposed 7 candidate including the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 is hereby declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The respondents Nos. 1- 4 are hereby directed to make proposal of 5(fives) senior most Additional Chief Engineers to the SSB without any special favour in favour of any particular candidate and to promote the most eligible candidate in terms of qualification, seniority and experience, on the basis of the ACR within 15 days of receipt of this judgment and order.</u>

End.
