full_judgment:
Md. Sirajul Islam, J: This rule under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff was directed against the judgment and decree dated 2.10.1994 passed by Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 191 of 1994 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 10.5.1994 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka rejecting the plaint of Title Suit No. 112 of 1994.

2. The petitioner as a plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 112 of 1994 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against the opposite parties for dissolution of partner and for accounts. The case of the plaintiff is that the defendant opposite party No. 1 took lease of the suit shop No. 15. Government New Market, Dhaka from the government and was carrying on business of cosmetics and stationery etc. in that shop. Subsequently defendant opposite party No. 1 entered into a contract with the plaintiff to carry on a partnership business for a period of 5 years in the said shop and that it was agreed upon between them to start a business in the shop in the name and style of M/S. Shams Jewelary. Accordingly, there was a written agreement between the parties dated 1st March, 1989 with condition amongst others that the 85% of the profit of partnership business will be received by plaintiff-petitioner and 15% of the profit will be received by defendant-opposite party no. 1 and also that defendant will get a monthly amount of Tk. 6000/-. It was further agreed upon that the petitioner having experience in the line of Jewelary business would carry on the business at his own risk an would provide cash for all purposes, maintaining accounts of the business and would provide the entire capital of the business and that the defendants opposite party no. 1 would simply decorate the shop at the cast of the petitioner. It was further stipulated in the agreement that the plaintiff petitioner would pay a sum of Tk. 6,50,000/- only to the defendant opposite party as security money which would be re-funded to the petitioner on the expiry of the partnership business. The plaintiff already paid the security amount of Tk. 6,50,000/- on proper receipt to the defendant and they started the partnership business of Jewlary in the said shop No. 15 at Government New Market, Dhaka. In the meantime, the term of 5 years ended on 28th February, 1994. Thereafter the defendant issued a notice dated 24.2.1994 directing the plaintiff to vacate the suit shop on 1st March, 1994 and expressed his desire to take possession of the suit shop. That the defendant did not render the accounts of partnership business and without rendering accounts he cannot oust the plaintiff-petitioner from the suit shop. The cause of action arose on 24.2.1994 and hence the plaintiff filed the suit for dissolution of the partnership and for accounts.

3. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed an application under Order 39 Rule I C.P.C. on 16.5.1994 praying for a temporary injunction for restraining the defendant from disturbing the plaintiff in his peaceful possession of the suit shop and for restraining him from evicting the plaintiff there from. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner entered into the plaint of the case and found that the plaintiff has got no case on the statements as made in the plaint as because his partnership business as per written agreement dated 1st March, 1989 has already expired before the filing of the suit and thus the learned Subordinate Judge came to the finding that the plaintiff has no cause of action for the suit against the defendants and on that finding, he rejected the plaint of the suit by order dated 16.5.1994. Against that judgment and order dated 16.5.1994 the plaintiff preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 191 of 1994 it the Court of District Judge, Dhaka which was heard and disposed of by Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. The learned Additional District Judge after hearing both the parties and considering all the facts and circumstances of the case came to a finding that the plaintiff has no cause of action, that the suit is in this form and that the plaintiff has possibility of getting any relief in the suit and accordingly the learned Additional District Judge dismissed the appeal and upheld the judgment and order of the trial court vide his judgment and order dated 2.10.1994.

4. Being aggrieved by this judgment and order dated 2.10.1994 passed by the Additional District Judge the plaintiff as a petitioner has filed this revisional application in this court and obtained the present rule.

5. Mr. Miah. Abdul Gafur, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner submits that the learned Subordinate Judge hastily rejected the plaintiff's plaint by his order dated 16.5.1994 without giving any opportunity to the plaintiff to make his submission fixing date for hearing the matter of rejection of the plaint. The learned Advocate submits that the learned Additional District Judge did not also consider this aspect of hastly rejection of the plaint nor did he consider the plaintiff's right to get an opportunity to cure the defect, if any, in the plaint and thus the learned Additional District Judge committed an error of law in coming to his decision which has occasioned a failure of justice to the plaintiff-petitioner.

6. Mr. Amjad Hossain the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-opposite party has, on the other hand, submitted that there is no hard and fast rule in respect of any stage for rejection of the plaint but that a plaint can be rejected at any stage even at the initial stage, if the plaint prima-facie does not disclose any cause of action in favour of the plaintiff. Mr. Amjad Hossain submits that the plaintiff's only case is a case of dissolution of partnership created by a deed of agreement for 5 years, but that the term of 5 years has already expired and accordingly as per the terms of the agreement the said partnership has been dissolved by lapse of .time. He refers to para 5 of the plaint and said that it has been stated in the plaint itself that the plaintiff has accepted this dissolution of partnership after the expiry of the fixed period of term of agreement. The learned Advocate submits that on this statement alone as made in the plaint it will appear that nothing is left for the court to dissolve the partnership and as such the plaintiff has no cause of action for bringing this suit.

7. Mr. Amjad Hossain next submits that so far as rendering the accounts of partnership is concerned as asked for in the plaint, it will appear that the whole accounts has been lying with the plaintiff himself as per the conditions laid down in the deed of agreement itself and as per statement itself made in the plaint also. He submits that the plaintiff was doing the business with the help of employees and was maintaining the bank account, cash account and all other matters relating to the accounts of the partnership business and the defendant no. 1 was simply receiving an amount of Tk. 6000/- per month as per term of the agreement from outside the shop and therefore, the defendant had nothing to render any account to the plaintiff.

8. We have gone through the plaint of the suit and we find that it has been stated in the plaint that the plaintiff would carry on business of Jewelary and would provide all cash for all sorts of transaction and expenditure and that he would maintain all accounts and carry on the business. It was further stated therein that the defendant would not invest any capital and he would simply decorate the shop with furniture and the plaintiff would provide the necessary capital for the same. It has further been stated that the plaintiff would pay a lump sum amount of Tk. 6000/- as profit per month to the defendant No. 1. Thus by a plain reading of the plaint it appears that the whole account of the Jewelary shop of the partnership business lies with the plaintiff himself and that he was in possession of the whole shop. Since he was in possession of the whole shop and was also in possession of whole account of the business of Jewelery, it was a matter for the plaintiff himself to render account but not the defendant because of the fact that the defendant was not in possession of the shop. We, therefore, agree with the contention as put forward by Mr. Amjad Hossain, the learned Advocate for the opposite party that the defendant has no business to render any accounts because he was not in charge of the account. In such facts and circumstances of the case we find that the plaintiff's suit was not maintainable in law and in fact for want of any cause of action against the defendant and that the plaintiff has no possibility of getting any relief of in the suit and as such, it is no use lingering a fruitless litigation between the parties.

9. Mr. Amjad Hossain, the learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite party in support of his contention that the plaint can be rejected at any stage, even at the initial stage, has referred to a few decisions in the case of Chowmuhani College and another Vs. Md. Ismail Hossain and others reported in 26 DLR 10, the case of Burma Eastern Ltd. Vs. Burmah Eastern Employees Union and others reported in 18 D.L.R. (Dac.) 709 and the case of Chairman, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka and other Vs. Motijheel Model High School and others reported in 46 DLR (HC) 485. The common principle as laid down in all cited cases is that

"the power of rejection of plaint shall be exercised only if the court comes to the conclusion on mere reading of the plaint that even if all the allegations are proved the plaintiff would no be entitled to any relief whatsoever. That the plaint can be rejected at any stage of the suit” In the above cited case reported in 18 DLR, it has been observed by their Lordships as under:-

"The principles under lying Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure are too fold: In the first place, it contemplates that a still-born suit should be properly buried, at its inception, so that no further time is consumed on a fruitless litigation. Secondly, it gives plaintiff a chance to his steps, at the earliest possible moment, so that if permissible under law, he may found a properly constituted case". To has further been held there in that "if the case does not come within the law of Order 7 Rule 11 C.P.C. then the court should, in such case, reject the plaint under its inherent power.

10. In the instant case before us it appears that the plaintiff's suit was a still-born suit and that the learned courts below rejected the plaint of the suit at its inception, not on any prayer under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure but under its inherent power. We are therefore of the opinion, that the principle laid down in the above cited cases will be the principle laid down in the above cited cases will be applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case rejecting the plaint under inherent power of the court.

11. Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner referred to a number of decisions in support of his contention that the plaintiff should not have been reject without giving the plaintiff a chance to cure the defect, if any in the plaint. He cited the decision in the case of Sk. Md. Jovoid and others Vs. Turner Morrision and Co. Ltd. reported in 26 DLR (HC) 111, the case of Guiness Peat (Trading) Ltd., Vs. Md. Fazlur Rahman reported in 44 DLR (AD) 242, case of Chairman, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Vs. Motijheel Model High School and others reported in 46 DLR (HC) 485. The common principles in respect of rejection of plaint as laid down by their Lordships in the above cited cases are as under:-

"Rejection of plaint under rule 11 of Order 7 C.P. Code does not preclude a fresh suit under rule 13. But still rejection of plaint should not be hastily made without affording an opportunity to the plaintiff either to cure the defect or to amend the plaint. The power of rejection of a plaint under Rule 11 shall be exercised only if the court comes to the conclusion on mere reading of the plaint that even if all the allegations are proved the plaintiff would not he entitled to any relief whatsoever".

<u>12. In the instant case before us, we have already stated above the facts and circumstances of the case from which it clearly appears that the plaintiff has no case of dissolution of partnership as because the plaintiff himself admitted in para 5 of the plaint that he accepted the dissolution due to the expiry of the period of agreement. As regards the accounts as sought for by the plaintiff in the plaint we have discussed above the facts and circumstances of the case and the statements made in the plaint and found that the plaintiff is responsible for the whole accounts of the suit-shop but not the defendant. Thus, the facts and circumstances of the case in the face of the plaint clearly go in show that the plaintiff's suit was not maintaining and that the plaintiff shall not be entitled to any relief whatsoever and that the plaintiff has no cause of action against the defendant and as such, the plaint is liable to be rejected in limini under the inherent power of the court in the interest of justice without wasting time and energy in such a fruitless litigation, as because this plaint as it stands is no plaint in the eye of law.</u>

13. By a perusal of the impugned judgment passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka, we find that the learned Judge has written a very exhaustive judgment in the matter of rejection of a plaint. He has elaborately discussed the conditions of agreement of 1st March, 1989 and the facts and circumstances as stated in the plaint itself and that he has also referred to the decision of 46 DLR as we have discussed above and then the learned Additional District Judge has come to the conclusion that although the plaint has been 'hastily' rejected by the trial court but still then the plaintiff as per statements of his plaint itself had no cause of action that his suit was not maintainable and that he had no probability of getting any relief in the suit whatsoever. In the facts and circumstances of the case as we have discussed above, we find that the learned Additional District Judge has correctly come to this finding and rightly passed the impugned judgment and order. There is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and order.

14. For all the reasons stated above the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The order of status-quo granted earlier by this court is hereby vacated.

15. Send down the L.C. record to the court concerned with a copy of this order.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Fazlul Karim, Advocate ------ For the petitioner.
Mr. Shahidul Islam, Advocate ------ For the opposite party.
parties:
Sanaullah @ Sonaullah Mollah ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Abdus Sattar Sheikh and ors ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Syed J.R. Mudassir Husain, J: This revisional application at the instance of the pre-emptor petitioner called in question the propriety of the Judgment and order dated 18.7.90 passed by the learned District Judge, Bogra in Misc. Appeal No. 13 of 1988 reversing those dated 9.11.87 passed in Misc. Case no. 66 of 1980 (pre-emption) by the learned Subordinate judge allowing the said pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

2. The short facts leading to the issuance of the rule are that the petitioner filed an application for pre-emption in respect of the case land measuring 1.82 acres which belonged to Basar Mullah. The pre-emptor petitioner and the opposite party no. 2 Alefa Bibi are co-sharers. The said opposite party no. 2 transferred the case land under pre-emption by a kabala dated 18.12.79 in favour of pre-emptee opposite party no. 1 Abdus Sattar who is a stranger to the case jute. It has been further stated that the pre-emptor came to learn about the said transfer on 1.3.1980 and filed the pre-emption case on 14.5.1980 being a co-sharer of opposite party no. 2.

3. The opposite party no. 2 Alefa Bibi contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing written objection stating inter alia that she being a childless widow used to reside in her father's house. She got 1.83 acres of land by way of inheritance. It has been further stated that the opposite party no. 1 (Sattar) used to call her (the opposite party no. 2) as Khala (aunt) and she wanted to mortgage some lands' to the said opposite party no. 1 but the opposite party no. 1 by practising fraud upon her got a kabala registered in respect of the entire property measuring 1.83 acres which was shown to have been transferred to him (the opposite party no. 10). She challenged the said transfer by filing a suit being Other Class Suit No. 211 of 1980 to declare the aforesaid transfer a product of fraud. The said suit was decreed on compromise by the decree dated 13.9.1980. By the said compromise decree, the deed under pre-emption was declared to be a deed without any consideration and not binding upon her the plaintiff of the said suit and the opposite party no. 2 herein. It was therefore contended that the above miscellaneous case of the petitioner is not maintainable since there is no existence of the deed under pre-emption.

4. The trial Court however allowed the pre-emption case considering the fact that the aforesaid Other Class Suit No. 211 of 1980 was filed after filing of the pre-emption case and as such the decree passed in the said other class suit no 211 of 1980 has not affected the right of pre-emption of the petitioner. The opposite party no. 2 Alefa Bibi filed an appeal and on appeal the learned District Judge allowed the same by reversing the judgment and order of the trial court below.

5. The pre-emptor petitioner, being aggrieved by the aforesaid decision of the appellate Court moved this court and obtained the present rule.

6. Mr. Fazlul Karim the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the judgment and decree in Other Class Suit No. 211 of 1980 does not affect the right of pre-emption on the ground that the said other class suit instituted during the pendency of the pre-emption proceeding wherein the pre-emptor was not made a party. He has further submitted that right of pre-emption being statutory right it cannot be taken away by any decree passed in a suit during the pendency of the pre-emption application.

7. It has been further submitted by Mr. Fazlul Karim that on the date of filing of the pre-emption case if the deed under pre-emption appeared to have existed, there cannot be any denial in allowing pre-emption and in support of this contention he has relied upon decision in the case of Meherjan wife of Amjad Ahmed Molla Vs. Jalal Ahmed Howlader and others reported in 13 DLR at page 612 and contends that the principle as laid down in the aforesaid decision fully applies in the instant case. Mr. Karim has pointed out that in the instant case the kabala under the pre-emption was executed and registered on 18.12.79, the pre-emption case was filed on 14.5.80, the Other Class Suit No. 211 of 1980 filed by the opposite party no. 2 Alefa Bibi against the opposite party no. 1 Abdus Sattar son of this petitioner on 1.7.80 for setting aside the sale deed dated 18.12.79 and there was a compromise decree obtained by the said opposite party no. 2 on 13.9.80. Having shown those dates Mr. Karim argued that during the pendency of the pre-emption proceeding, the decree as obtained by this vendor cannot affect the pre-emption case as the same was filed earlier. Moreover, in the said suit the pre-emptor was not made a party and as such the said decree cannot be binding upon the petitioner. With reference to the above dates Mr. Karim further argued that the facts of the case reported in 13 DLR are quite identical with the facts of the instant case and as such the learned District Judge ought to have affirmed the decision of the trial court.

8. Mr. Karim has further submitted that it is the consistent view of the Appellate Division that the deed of re-conveyance if made for taking away the right of pre-emption or if any reconveyance was found to be colourable one for frustrating the right of pre-emption that cannot effect the right of pre-emption. In support of his above point. Mr. Karim has relied upon a decision in the case of Shafi Khan vs. Mannujan reported in 35 DLR(AD) at page 225.

9. Mr. Shahidul Islam the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties on the other hand submits that the kabala under pre-emption dated 18.12.79 have been found to be forged one as per the decree obtained by the opposite party no. 2 Alefa Bibi in Other Class Suit No. 211 of 1980 and as such there was no transfer in the eye of law and the suit land returned back to the vendor therefore the pre-emption application became not pre-emptor himself admitted in his deposition that the deed under the pre-emption has been obtained by his son opposite party no. 1 by practising fraud upon the vendor and the opposite party no. 1 was none but the son of the pre-emptor. In view of such admission the pre-emptor's whole case has been demolished. With regard to the facts of the case reported in 13 D.L.R. and those of the instant case are quite different and distinguishable because of the fact that in 13 DLR case the deed under pre-emption was not challenged to be a forged one having been obtained by practising fraud in the name of getting registered mortgage deed. But in the instant case it is the specific case of the pre-emptee opposite party no. 2 that opposite party no. 1 got the deed under pre-emption by practising fraud upon her in getting a registered kabala instead of getting registered mortgage deed and for which she had to file the aforesaid Other Class Suit No. 211 of 1980 for setting aside the said kabala and it was ended in a compromise decree and the sale was set aside and the opposite party no. 2 Alefa Bibi got back her land.

10. Mr. Islam has further pointed out in 13 DLR Case the pre-emptor did not admit the deed under pre-emption to be an illegal and forged deed but in the instant case the pre-emptor himself as P.W. has admitted the deed under pre-emption to be a forged deed by stating the following facts- “আলেফা আমার ভাতিজি হয়। আমরা বাসার মোল্লার সম্পত্তি বন্টন করিয়া নিয়াছি। আলেফা ঐ দলিল মূলে ১.৮৩ শতক সম্পত্তি প্রাপ্ত হয়। আমরা মামলার জমি ১.৮৩ শতক এবং নালিশী দলিলে ১.৮৩ শতক আছে। সাত্তার আলেফাকে টাকা দেওয়া দেখিনি। ছাত্তার .১৫ শতক খায় খালাসী লওয়ার কথা বলিয়া ফাকি দিয়া আলেফার সমস্ত সম্পত্তি কবলা করিয়া নেয়।

11. Mr. Shahidul Islam has further pointed out that 13 DLR's case the pre-emption as filed on 3.6.57, summons was served upon the pre-emptee on 11.7.57, Title Suit was filed on 15.7.57 with view to frustrate the result of the pre-emption case, compromise was effected on 9.11.57 and pre-emptor wanted to be added as a party in the title suit on 5.12.57. But the said application was rejected and the title suit was decreed. But in the instant case, the pre-emption was filed on 4.5.80 summons were served upon the pre-emptee on 15.7.81, O.C. Suit No. 211 of 1980 was filed on 1.7.80 i.e. long before receiving summons of the pre-emption case and the O.C. suit was compromised on 13.9.80 that is before receiving summons of the pre-emption case. Thus in the instant case the O.C. Suit No. 211 of 1980 was filed and the decree was passed before the summons of the pre-emption case was served upon the pre-emptee. In the instant case there is no averment in the pre-emption application that the pre-emptee No. 2 after coming to know of filing of the pre-emption case, had filed the O.C. Suit No. 211 of 1980 and also there is no evidence on record that the pre-emptee No. 2 with a view to frustrate the right of pre-emption, has got the deed under pre-emption set aside by a show up decree.

12. Mr. Islam has also pointed out that in the 13 DLR's case the payment of consideration was made against the deed under the pre-emption But in the instant case the pre-emptor himself admitted in his evidence that “ছাত্তার আলেফাকে টাকা দেওয়া দেখি নাই” and there is no other evidence on record to show that Sattar purchased the land making payment of consideration rather it appears from exhibit A the certified copy of the compromise decree passed in O.C. Suit No. 211 of 1980 that no consideration was paid against the deed under pre-emption. Further it appears that the pre-emptor himself has admitted the fact that “ছাত্তার .১৫ শতক খায় খালাশী হওয়ার কথা বলিয়া ফাকি দিয়া আলেফার সমস্ত সম্পত্তি কবলা করিয়া নেয়।” son no consideration was passed against the deed under pre-emption rather the deed under pre-emption was obtained by fraud.

13. Apart from this aspect, Mr. Shahidul Islam, in my view has rightly argued that by the compromise decree vide ext. A arising out of the aforesaid suit filed by the vendor opposite party No. 2 Alefa Bibi got back her land and there remains nothing for the petitioner to pre-empt and on this ground alone, the principle as laid down in the case reported in 13 DLR cannot be applied in the instant case.

14. Mr. Shahidul Islam then pointed out with regard to the decision reported in 35 D.L.R. (AD) page 225 of to the effect that it was held in that case that if the transaction is a colourable one or a mere paper transaction, then there has been no real transfer and as such the pre-emption right will prevail. But in the instant case it was not pleased that the judgment and decree passed in O.C. Suit No. 211 of 1980 was colourable one. So the case reported in 35 D.L.R. (AD) has also got no manner of application in the instant case.

15. I have gone through the decisions as referred to above by Mr. Fazlul Karim. It appears from the record that P.W. I the pre-emptor himself admitted that the deed under pre-emption was not a kabala deed on admitting the following facts

“ছাত্তার .১৫ শতক খায় খালাশী হওয়ার কথা বলিয়া ফাকি দিয়া আলেফার সমস্ত সম্পত্তি কবলা করিয়া নেয়।”

It further appears that by the compromise decree dated 13.8.80 passed in O.C. Suit No. 211 of 1980 the opposite party No. 1 admitted the deed under pre-emption is a forged deed and not a kabala deed. It will not be out of place to refer to the contents of exhibit A the certified copy of the compromise decree dated 13.9.80 passed in O.C. Suit No. 211 of 1980 which runs as under-

“বিবাদী স্বীকার করে যে ১-৪নং তফশিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি সমূহ বাবদ বিবাদীর নামীয় ইংরেজী ১৮-১২-৭৯ তারিখে নালিশী কবলা দলিল, তঞ্চকী, যোগসাজসী ষড়যন্ত্রমূলক, মূল্যবিহীন, পশু ও অকার্য্যাকারী বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে এবং উক্ত দলিলে উল্লেখিত কনসিডারেশন মানি বিবাদী বরাবর প্রদান করে নাই এবং উক্ত দলিল সূত্রে বিবাদী নালিশী সম্পত্তি সমূহের কোন দিন কোন স্বত্ব দখল লাভ করে নাই। ইহাও বিবাদী স্বীকার করিল। বিবাদী আরও স্বীকার করে যে, নালিশী ১-৪নং তফশীল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি সমূহের বাদীনির একক স্বত্ব দখল বিদ্যমান রহিয়াছে।

<u>16. Considering the admission of pre-emptor (P.W.1) and the contents of the said Ext. A I find that in the deed under pre-emption, no land was transferred in favour of the alleged transferred opposite party No. 1 herein. Therefore, the alleged deed of transfer cannot be construed to be a kabala and moreover, it is found that the said deed has been created by practising fraud upon the vendor the opposite party No. 2 and the fraud has vitiated everything.</u>

17. Having regarded to above discussion, I find substance in the contention raised by Mr. Shahidul Islam as he has rightly distinguished the facts of the instance case from those of the cited cases. Therefore hold that the deed under pre-emption is not pre-emptiable since vendor got back the land by a compromise decree.

18. For that reasons stated above I find no illegality has been committed by the court of appeal below and the judgment and order of the appellate court is hereby affirmed.

19. In the result, the rule is discharged and no order is made as to costs.

Send down the L.C. Record at once.

End.

Vs.
The Chairman, Board of Directors, Dhaka Water Supply

full_judgment:
K M Hassan, J: The Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause why the memo No.102/MODS fated 6.5.98 an contained in Annexure-D to the Writ Petition shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why the respondents shall not be directed to rescind the same and proceed in accordance with the term of the Tender Documents.

2. The facts as stated in the petition in short are that the petitioner No.1 is a private limited company engaged in the business of trading exporting importing and supply of specialized equipment's. The petitioner No. 2 is the managing director of the petitioner No.1 company.

3. The Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority statutory corporate body hereinafter called the 'Authority' is the respondent No. 4 It has a Board of Directors appointed by the Government. Its Chairman is also appointed by the Government and a Member of Parliament belonging to the ruling party is also a member of the Board of Directors. The Board takes policy decision as and when necessary but the Managing Director is the Chief Executive Officer of the 'Authority' and the 'Authority' runs and functions under his day to day guidance and supervision. It is claimed by the petitioner that the appointees in the Board often interfere with the internal management of the authority.

4. By a Tender Notice issued on behalf of the respondents bids wore invited for supply of twenty nine sewerage pump motors for different sewerage lift stations under a project called "Urgent Sewerage Rehabilitation and Expansion Project Package-II" hereinafter called the "Project.

5. The bids for the first call were submitted on 27.4.97 but as all the bids were found technically non-responsive a second tender was called and the bids were submitted on 25.6.97 in which four bidders participated including the petitioner No. 1 and the respondent No. 5. The Technical Evaluation Committee had found the respondent No. 5 non-responsive on the pound that it had made two offers in the same bid. The bid of the petitioner No. 1 was also found non-responsive and was rejected on a very minor pretext because of political pressure. The pretext was that the petitioner No. 1 did not offer the bid bond for 150 days though in the schedule of the tender document the bid bond was required to be furnished within 120 days. Accordingly third tender notice dated 14.7.97 was advertised in the newspaper which was published on 15.7.97 and the bids were submitted oh an extended date i.e. 12.8.97 at 12 noon. The bidders submitted their tenders in two separate sealed packets one containing the Technical Proposal and the other containing the Financial Proposal. While the Technical Proposals were opened and sent to the technical Evaluation Committee for evaluation and report the Financial Proposals were kept in safe custody of the respondent No. 2 (Annexures A and A-1.). Thereafter the 'Authority' maintained a long silence for More than six months. By a letter dated 10.2.98 the petitioner and the respondent No. 5 were asked by the 'Authority' to produce samples of pump within 60 days for testing by the Engineering University, BUET (Annexure -13-).The petitioners were surprised by the letter as it did not specify which one of the eight kind of pumps invited by the tender. was required to be tested. The petitioner's claim that this was done in violation of the condition of the terms and conditions of the tender document because there is no provision in it for testing samples once the bids have been submitted. Moreover such testing would cost a huge amount of money out of the budget of the petitioner accordingly the petitioner raised objection by letter dated 15.2.98 (Annexure-"B but nevertheless agreed to submit samples of motor as asked for. It is further staled in the petition that in their bid the petitioners proposed to supply world famous KSB pumps made in Germany and the respondent No. 5 proposed to supply pumps made in India. In another bid previously invited by the same 'Authority' for supply of pumps and awarded to the respondent No. 5 the latter supplied Indian pumps which were found not to be satisfactory as all the pumps were burnt within two months of their use.

6. The respondents however, did not pursue the proposal for testing and did not send any  reply to the letter written by the petitioners but pursuant to a decision of the Board they unofficially enquired of the petitioners whether they would be agreeable to divide the work between the qualified bidders. The petitioners by a letter dated 20.4.98 agreed to the proposal so that a quick decision could be obtained (Annexure-'C').

7. In the meantime the petitioners were waiting for the Technical Evaluation Committee Report which would determine the technically qualified bidders under the terms of the tender documents. Clauses 13, 14 and 15 of the tender document specifically provide that only those bids which will conform to the requirements and specifications of the Department will be considered as responsive. The Technical Proposal will be evaluated according to the criterion given in clause 15 Part-C of the tender document. According to the clause ally bidder obtaining minimum 60 points shall be treated technically qualified. Once the bids are determined technically qualified only then the Financial Proposals of the bidders will be considered.

8. While the petitioners were waiting for the report of the Technical Evaluation Committee all of a sudden on 6.5.98 at about 3.45 P.M. the petitioners were served with a letter dated 6.5.98 under Memo No. 102/MODS signed by the Respondent No. 3 conveying that the Financial Proposals of the petitioners and that of the respondent No. 5 would be opened at 12 P.M. on 10.5.98. The aforesaid letter did not specify whether the Technical Proposal of the petitioner for the respondent No. 5 or any other bidder has been found responsive for consideration of the Financial Proposal (Annexure-D).

9. The petitioners claim that they have come to learn that the Technical Evaluation Committee have submitted their report and found three bids non-responsive including that of the respondent No. 5 on the ground that the respondent No. 8 offered 'Semi Drip Proof Motors' instead of 'Drip Proof as required under the tender document. Moreover the respondent No. 5 did not submit the correct papers to match their specification. They supplied information regarding their manufacture on a piece of paper which had no monogram and address of the manufacturer on it. According to the petitioners all these information were squired to be supplied in a printed catalogue as per the terms of the Tender document. But despite all those the respondent in collusion with the respondent No. 5 has been proceeding to open be Financial Proposal so that the work could be awarded to the respondent No. 5. The petitioners claim that as the tender bid of the respondent No. 5 was not supported by any authentic document it violated clause 1(g) and 13(V) and. 14(i) of part-C of the Tender Document. It is further claimed that the proposal for opening of the Financial Proposal without releasing the report of the Technical Evaluation Committee amounts to violation of the terms of the Tender document.

10. The petitioners served a Demand of Justice Notice upon the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 but received no reply from the respondents (Annexure-F).

11. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned order the petitioners moved this Court and obtained this Rule.

12. Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 the Managing Director, Water Supply and Sewerage Authority (WASA) and the Superintending Engineer and Project Director, MODS Circle Dhaka WASA. respectively by jointly filing an affidavit-in-opposition denied the material allegations and claimed that though the member of the Board were nominated by the government in accordance with WASA Ain, 1996 from among professionals yet the Board never interferes with the functioning and internal management of the 'Authority' as alleged in the writ petition. It simply formulates the policy and leaves the Management to the Managing Director. It is further stated that Khan Tipu Sultan a Member of Parliament has been made a member of the Board not as a Member of Parliament but as an elected member of the Bangladesh Bar Council as per section 6 of Dhaka WASA Ain, 1996. It is further claimed that the Chief Executive of the WASA is the Managing Director who is solely responsible for the internal management of the "Authority' under the provisions of WASA Ain of 1996. The respondents further assert that no political pressure and patronization on the Technical Evaluation Committee was over exercised. It is further claimed that because of their participation in the third tender notice the petitioner should not have any grievance. In the third call two tenders namely the tender of the writ petitioner and that of the respondent No. 5 were found technically responsive but as it was the third call the Managing Director asked the convenor of the Technical Evaluation Committee to contact all the bidders. Accordingly the convenor of the Technical Evaluation Committee contacted the bidders for clarification and submission of further papers. When the Technical Evaluation Committee was not satisfied with the written explanation the matter was placed before the WASA Board in its meeting held on 19.1.98 and the Board 'decided that the technically responsive bidder would be asked to supply samples of pump within 60 days to be tested by BUET. The respondent No. 5 agreed to the proposal but the writ petitioner by its letter dated 15.2.98 raised objection but at the same time agreed to send samples for test provided they were given four months time.

13. Subsequently the writ petitioner and the respondent No. 5 by two separate letters dated 20.4.98 intimated that they were ready to share the work if the 'Authority' gave them the work. Therefore, it is absolutely false to say that the petitioner 'were unofficially asked by the Board to inform whether they would agree to share the work with respondent No. 5 with regard to the allegations that twenty pumps previously supplied by the respondent No. 5 to the authority were burnt it is stated that those pumps were submersible water pumps whereas the instant pumps are sewerage turbine pumps (Annexure 1-VII). The proposal from the writ petitioners and the respondent No. 5 to divide the work between them was placed before the Board in its meeting held on 23.4.98 and after threadbare discussion it was decided that financial offers of the technical responsive bidders would be opened and the work order would be awarded to the lowest bidder. Accordingly the date for opening of the bid was fixed at 12-00 noon on 10.5.98.

14. It is further stated that all the members of the Technical Evaluation Committee except one who was abroad evaluated the technical offers of all the five bidders and found the bids of the writ petitioners and the respondent No. 5 technically responsive. It is also stated that the tender document does a not provide for forwarding report of the Technical Evaluation Committee to the bidders as contended by the writ petitioners. Moreover the satisfaction of the technical committee cannot be challenged or called in question in any court of law.

15. It is further stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that in the report submitted by the Technical Evaluation Committee the respondent No. 5 was found technically responsive though there was some confusion whether the motors proposed to be supplied by them were drip proof or not. However in the final report after consulting technical literature the same were found to be drip proof. Therefore the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 contend that the submission of the petitioner that the respondent No. 5 offered to supply 'Semi Drip Proof Motor instead of 'Drip Proof Motor' is not correct.

16. It is claimed that the technical details of the respondent No. 5's bid were mentioned on the continuation sheet of the manufacturer duly signed and sealed by them. Moreover the manufacturer subsequently authenticated the said technical offer. Annexure IX(e) and IX(b). As both the petitioners and respondent No. 5 were found technically responsive a decision was taken to open the financial offers by the impugned letter. The name of the work being "Urgent Sewerage Rehabilitation and Expansion (Package-II it needed to be completed within 30th June, 1999 otherwise the fund would have lapsed.

17. Respondent No. 5 by filing affidavit-in-opposition denied the material allegations and supported the case of the respondent Nos. 2 and 3.

18. Mr. Moudud Ahmed learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the impugned order dated 6.5.98 showing the respondent No. 5 a responsive bidder is unlawful. The reasons are as follows:

(1) The respondent No. 5 has failed to submit the relevant papers for example. Catalogue Brochure and Technical Data while submitting the Technical Proposal. The very fact that an authentication became necessary and that the letter of authentication dated 13.10. 97 was sent by the manufacturer (Annexure-EX(b) to the affidavit-in-opposition of the Respondent Nos. 2 and 3) containing not only the authentication but offering of various options sufficiently prove that the respondent No. 5 had failed to comply with Clause 1(G). part-C and Clause 13(v)4 of the tender document.

(2) Since the respondent No. 5 has failed to comply with and fulfill all aspects of the specifications required wider Clause 14(i) of the Tender Document their bid was non-responsive from the very beginning. The tender bid of the respondent No. 5 should have been rejected immediately on submission of the first report of the Evaluation Committee on 2.9.97 which found the respondent No. 5 non responsive for offering semi Drip Proof Motor' instead of 'Drip Proof Motor'.

(3) In the third call the bids of three other participants whose tender were similar to that of the respondent No. 5 were also rejected on the ground that they did not comply with the terms of the tender document. Therefore the selection of the bid of the respondent No. 5 as responsive was arbitrary.

(4) The letter of WASA dated W.2.98 for supply of pumps for sample, testing is violative of the terms of the tender document and proves that the respondent No. 5 was not considered as a responsive bidder.

19. Mr. Moudud Ahmed further submits that the Financial Proposal cannot be opened till the completion of the first stage by evaluation of the technical proposal in accordance with Article 15. Part-C of the bid document. Therefore entering into second phase without completing the first stage is illegal.

20. He further claims that the authority was influenced politically and referred to a letter dated 18.1.98 (Annexure-x) sent by the Ministry of Local Government addressed to the Managing Director. WASA wherein a letter dated 5.01.96 issued by the Prime Minister's Secretariat in connection with the tender has been referred to he also drew our attention to another letter written by a Minister of the High Commission of India. Dhaka dated 4.1.98 (Annexure X-l) to the Managing Director of WASA requesting him to give due consideration to the bid of the Respondent No. 5. This letter was sent just before the meeting of the Board of Directors held on 19.1.98. The WASA was thus influenced politically in passing the impugned order. In this connection he has referred to a case reported in 27 DLR 1975 page 649.

21. On the question of locus standi Mr. Moudud Ahmed has, submitted that it is now a settled issue that where the executive authority in exercise of statutory power creates an inchoate right in favour of a person and that person becomes aggrieved due to any abuse of power or violation of the terms of the tender he is entitled to seek protection of law tinder the writ jurisdiction.. On the question of locus standi he has referred us to the cases reported in AIR 1979 (SC) 1628. AIR 1982 (Cal.)19: 27 DLR 649: 32 DLR(AD) 223. 37 DLR(AD) 117: 39 DLR 78: 40 DLR(AD) 62 and 47 DLR 515.

22. Mr. M.A. Wahab Mia the learned Advocates representing respondent Nos. 2 and 3 assails the submission of Mr. Moudud Ahmed by stating that WASA is a statutory authority and in the instant case it has acted with a bonafide intention for public interest, to improve the existing water supply condition at the earliest possible time. The Managing Director is in-charge of its day today function and the Board never interferes with the Managing Directors function nor was there any political pressure or diplomatic influence. The Authority acted independently on the basis of the opinion received from the Technical Evaluation Committee.

23. The learned Advocate then con-tends that though in the writ petition the acceptance of the report of the Technical Evaluation Committee has been challenged but the Rule itself was issued in different term challenging the opening of the Financial Proposal. Further the members of the Technical Evaluator Committee on whose report the hid of the respondent No. 5 was found technically responsive were not made parties even though it is claimed that WASA's action was malafide. Moreover by agreeing to share the work with the respondent No. 5 the petitioners have waived their right if there was any. He also submits that there is no violation of any clause of the tender document and by clause 12 the 'Authority' has reserved the right to reject any tender document. Lastly, the petitioner did not acquire any legal right by submitting the tender document.

24. Mr. Mahmudul Islam the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 5 submits that the writ petition involves questions of fact resolution of which is not possible by this court in exercise of its writ jurisdiction as such the writ petition is liable to be discharged in limini. He argues that expert opinion is necessary to challenge the report of the Technical Evaluation Committee but taking of such evidence is not possible in the writ jurisdiction.

25. He also argues that the dispute being raised in respect of an ordinary commercial contract it is not amenable to the writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. A simple contractual right cannot be enforced against a public functionary, Moreover the writ petition is barred by the principles of waiver acquiescence and estoppel and in the facts and circumstances of the case this writ petition is not maintainable.

26. The learned Advocate further submits that there is nothing in the tender form on which it can be said that the request of the authority for supply of the specimen pumps is contrary to the tender terms and in any view of the matter this has no relevancy since the petitioner agreed to supply specimen pumps. Lastly, it is not open to the petitioners to question the judgment of the Technical Evaluation Committee.

27. At the very outset let us decide the preliminary objection taken that this writ petition is not maintainable as contractual right cannot be enforced against public functionaries.

28. It too contended on behalf of the respondents that a public functionary has absolute discretion to accept one tender and reject another. Even it its decision is wrong such a decision cannot be challenged in a writ petition as no legal right of the petitioner has been m or infringed by such decision of the authority.

29. Mr. Moudud Ahmed the learned Advocate for the petitioner on the other hand assailed the submission by arguing that in recent years the writ jurisdiction in case of a contract entered into by a corporation or an agent of Government has been widened to such extent that the preliminary objection of the respondents on the ground of maintainability is liable to be rejected in limini. In this connection he has referred us to several cases which are already mentioned above.

30. He heavily relies on D.F.D. South Kheri Vs. Ran Sanehi reported in AIR 1973(SC) 205. In this case it is held that where an action of the public authority invested with statutory powers is challenged the writ petition is maintainable even if the right to relief arises out of en alleged broach of contract. In para 4 it is observed.

"We are unable to hold that merely because the source of the right which the respondent claims was initially in a contract for obtaining relief against any arbitrary and unlawful action on the part of a public authority he must resort to a suit and not to a petition by way of writ".

In support of his contention Mr. Ahmed further cites the case of Ramana Vs international Airport Authority of India AIR 1979 (SC) 1628 wherein it has been observed in pare 20

"Now Obviously whole a corporation is an instrumentality or agency of Governments it would in the exercise of its power or discretion be subject to the same constitutional or public law limitations as Government. The rule inhibiting arbitrary action by Government which we have discussed above must apply equally where such corporation is dealing with the public. whether by way of giving jobs or entering into contracts or otherwise and it cannot act arbitrarily and miter into relationship with any person it likes at its sweet will but its action must be in conformity with some principle which meets the test of reason and relevance."

31. He has also referred us to 48 DLR(AD) 20 in which case a writ petition involving a commercial contract was held maintainable by the Appellate Division.

32. We have considered the submissions and gone through the papers annexed to the petition and the decisions referred to before us by both sides. In the case of Shaming Matchajibi Samabaya Sanity Ltd. Vs. Bangladesh end ors reported in 39 DLR (AD) 85 the following have been observed in paragraphs 28 and 29:-

Para 28.

Modern government has multifarious activities. Some of its functions are Governmental function while exercising sovereign power and again scene of the functions can be described as trading functions. To put it in plain language when the Government after accepting the tender places an order for supplying say for ten thousand chairs and the supplier agreed to do so a contract is entered into there is offer and its acceptance backed by obligations. Full-fledged contract conies into existence. Here the Government functions in the capacity as a trader e.g. an ordinary buyer if there is a breach of such contract the aggrieved party can sue for damages or any other appropriate remedy. But not by way of invoking writ jurisdiction.

Para 29.

On the other hand when the Government grant lease. Privilege, settlement etc. the Government act and discharges sovereign function "performing function in connection with affairs of the republic or the local authority". Such function can best be appreciated if matters of settlement of hat bazar fisheries khas land etc. are kept in view. The Government acts in these affairs in pursuance of some statutory power and any such contract when rooted in statute the Government discharges its sovereign function. While doing so if there is a breach of any statute or rule the same can be remedied by invoking writ jurisdiction. Even if any discretion is left in the statute such discretion must be exercised in accordance with settled principles and not arbitrarily.

<u>33. This Court has consistently applied the principles laid down in the above mentioned case except in it solitary decision of the High Court Division reported in 47 DLR 515. No deviation has also been made in the case of Bangladesh Telecom (Pvt.) Ltd. Vs. T & T. reported in 48 DLR (AD) 211 referred to by Mr. Moudud Ahmed. In this case Bangladesh Telecom (PVT) Ltd. entered into a written agreement dated 26.7.80 with Bangladesh Telegraph and Telephone Board. This agreement was a memorandum of understanding executory in nature. Subsequently, the agreement merged with a license granted on 25.3.90 to BTL under section 4 of the Telegraph Act. 1985 by BTB which was empowered by section 3 of the Bangladesh Telegraph and Telephone Board Ordinance 1979 to grant such a license. The licence was granted pursuant to and as sot out in detail in the agreement entered into on 26th July 1989 by and between BTTB and BTL. In other words the terms and conditions of the agreement dated 26.7.89 became the terms and conditions of license itself. It is held that when the terms and conditions of such a contract are merged into the license granted in exercise of statutory power a writ petition cannot be resisted on the ground of it being a commercial contract since the cancellation of the agreement will amount to cancellation of the license which was granted to in exercise of a statutory power. Tie cancellation of the license can be made only in exercise of the statutory power. If there was no license in favour of the Bit then the agreement would have been a purely commercial contract the cancellation of which would not have attracted the writ jurisdiction. Therefore in the facts and law points involved the case is not applicable in the instant case.</u>

<u>34. Mr. Moudud Ahmed has argued that a person can always come to the writ jurisdiction whenever an inchoate right created in his favour has been violated by executive exercise. An in-charge right means a right that has just begun but not yet developed into maturity. According to the principle of inchoate right even if the appellants bid is not the highest but if it is found that the highest offer suffers from any infirmity and has been accepted in violation of the terms and conditions of the tender then it stands rejected in which case the appellant’s offer will be the highest and valid conferring on him a right. In this connection he has referred to 32 DLR (AD) 223. 37 DLR(AD) 117 and in the case of Mozaher Sowdagar Vs. Zahurul Alam reported in 40 DLR(AD) 62. A study of these cases show that in all those cases appeals were preferred before the Appellate Division against judgments and orders passed in Civil Revision and not in writ petition. Therefore decisions hold in those cases is also not applicable in this case. The petitioners' remedy lies in civil suit and not in writ jurisdiction. The latest legal position laid down by our Supreme Court is that a dispute raised in an ordinary commercial contract oven though a statutory body is a party to the contract and an inchoate right is violated by executive exercise is not amenable to the writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution.</u>

35. In view of the above we do not think that this Court should interfere at this stage when no legal right has accrued in favour of the petitioner.

36. The Rule is discharged without any order as to costs for not being maintainable. Stay order granted earlier is vacated.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Abdul Quddus, J: This Civil Revision under section 115 C.P.C. at the instance of petitioner Mozammel Hoque is directed against order dated 10.9.98 by Election Tribunal, Jaldhaka, District Nilpahamari in Election Tribunal case No. 1 of 1998 allowing petition of opposite party No. 1 (original petitioner) Mohammad Ali for recountirg of ballot papers cast in the chairman election of Kaimari Union Parishad held on 1.12.97 in which present petitioner was declared elected as Chairman.

2. Opposite party No. 1 Mohammad Ali as petitioner filed Election Tribunal Case No. 1 of 1998 in the Court of Election Tribunal (Assistant Judge) Jaldhaka, Nilphamari for declaration that the Union Parishad election for Chairman of Kaimari Union Parishad held on 13.12.97 was void and for declaring the opposite party No. 1 Mohammad Ali as petitioner in the said election tribunal case as elected Chairman after recounting of the ballot papers cast in the said Chairman election of the Union Parishad. There were 5 candidates for the post of Chairman in the said election and there were 9 polling centres. It was alleged in the said election tribunal case by the present opposite party No. 1 Mohammad Ali as petitioner that his polling agents were forcibly pushed out from 4 centres such as No. 1 Changemari government primary school centre, No. 2. Binnayakhri High School, No. 3 Gabrol Siddiqua Government Primary School Centre, No. 4. Rotherdanqa Government Primary School centre by men main opposite party present petition Muzammel Haque in collusion with respective presiding officers of those polling cent, at the time of counting ballot papers, counter was collusively and illegally made to declar elected the present petitioner as opposite party No. 1 in the election tribunal case 1 of 1998 causing the present opposite party No. 1 as petitioner in the original election tribunal case, defeated by 8 votes. It was also alleged that in the election tribunal case that in No.2 Gabrol Siddiky Government primary school centre votes for some dead persons were cast fraudulently in collusion with the presiding office of the polling centre. It was alleged that if the ballot papers were property recounted original petitioner in the election tribunal case (present opposite party No. 1) would have been elected chairman of the said union parishad.

3. Present petitioner as opposite party No. 1 in the original election tribunal case appeared and filed written objection denying all material allegations and stating that the allegations were absolutely false, misleading and malafide and the election was absolutely free and fair and no false votes or invalid votes were cast and that the counting was correct') made. Both sides examined and cross exam fined witnesses at the final hearing. After conclusion of evidence original petitioner (present opposite party No. 1) Mohammad Ali filed a petition on 10.8.98 praying for recounting of ballot papers cast in the election held on 13.12.97 at the gunny bags with the ballot papers were received by the officer of the court from the Thana Nirbahi Officer as Returning officer on requisition at the prayer of the original petitioner. Present petitioner. as opposite party No. 1 in the original Election Tribunal case filed written objection on 17.8.98 praying for rejection of the prayer for recounting of ballot papers of the original petitioner (present opposite party No. 1). After hearing both sides learned election tribunal allowed the prayer for recounting of ballot papers of the original petitioner and rejected the objection filed by present petitioner as opposite party No. 1 in the original election tribunal case vide impugned order dated 10.9.98. Being aggrieved original opposite party No. 1 Mozammel Haque as present petitioner preferred this civil revision and obtained the rule.

4. Record was not called for. The opposite party No. 1 (original petitioner) Mohammad Ali was notified. Further proceeding of the Election Tribunal Case 1 of 1998 was stayed first for 3 months and subsequently stay order was extended till disposal of the Rule. Opposite Party No. I (original petitioner) Mohammad Ali appeared through engaged advocate contested the Rule and filed a special petition supported by an affidavit to vacate the stay order and also to discharge the rule on the ground that the impugned order dated 10.9.98 is not amenable to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 C.P.C. as the election tribunal is not a civil court in true sense. The case being otherwise ready was put for final hearing.

5. At the hearing learned Advocate for the present petitioner submits that immediately after the polling and the counting of votes no petition was filed nor any objection was raised by the present opposite party No. 1 as original petitioner in the election tribunal case to the respective presiding officers of the polling canters about any mal practices as regards polling and counting of votes as alleged claiming for recounting, then on subsequent allegation either in the main election petition or by any such petition filed afterwards by original petitioner for recounting of ballot papers there can not be any direction from the election tribunal for such recounting. He thus assails the impugned order dated 10.9.98 by which learned election tribunal illegally allower in spite of serious objection and erroneously directed for recounting of ballot papers. In that regard learned Advocate refers to the decision reported in 48DLR (AD) page 59 wherein it was held that in the absence of any prayer for recounting immediately after the polling before the presiding officer and also in the absence of any justification the recounting of ballot papers should not have been ordered. Learned Advocate also relies in this regard on the decisions reported in 48 DLR page 560, 38 DLR(AD) page 273 and 28 DLR page 375 as according to him similar view was taken in all above decisions. He refers to the certified copy of the original election petition of the tribunal case No. 1 of 1998 filed along with the revisional application as annexure A and submits that no where in the election petition the opposite party No. 1 Mohammad Ali an original petitioner stated anything that he made any allegation in that regard to the presiding officer of the polling centre immediately after the polling and counting claiming for recounting of ballot papers. He contends that subsequent disclosure of such allegation to the Returning Officer or in the election petition will not be enough for direction for recounting in view of decision reported in 48 DLR(AD) page 59 as noticed above. As regards maintainability of this civil revision under section 115 C.P.C. learned Advocate refers to the decision reported in 38 DLR(AD) page 172 wherein it was held that District Judge as an election appellate tribunal is not a persona designata, but a court subordinate to the High Court Division. He submits that the appeal is the continuation of the original proceeding and if the District Judge acting as an election appellate tribunal is subordinate to the High Court Division and its order and decision in such election appellate tribunal matter be amenable to the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 C.P.C. then the order passed in such election tribunal proceeding by the election tribunal judge consequently should also be amenable to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 C.P.C. in as much as the election tribunal appeal will be treated to be the continuation of the original election tribunal case. He contends that the present civil revision under section 115 C.P.C. will be legally maintainable. He earnestly submits that the impugned order of recounting dated 10.9.98 suffers from legal infirmity and error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice calling for interference by this court. According to him the rule should be made absolute.

6. In reply to above contentions raised by the present petitioner learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 1 Mohammad Ali (original petitioner in election tribunal case) submits that the decision reported in 48 D.L.R (AD) page 59 as referred to and cited on behalf of present petitioner will not hold good in view of latest decision on the point reported in 4BLC(AD)1999 page 209 wherein it was held that although no objection regarding counting of invalid votes was raised at the time of counting of votes but omission to raise such objection is no bar to challenge the result of an election in an election petition as such objection gives rise to an election dispute which is within the province of election tribunal to direct recounting of votes. He also refers to certified copy of the original petition of Election Tribunal Case No. 1 of 1998 filed with the revisional petition as Annexure A and shows that averments from paragraph Nos. 2,3,4 and 5 of the election petition that in collusion with presiding officers of 4 polling centres Mozammel Hoque opposite party No. 1 in the original petition committed practices in counting of votes by pushing out the agents of the original petitioner from the polling centres in order to cause defeat to the original petitioner by a difference of 8 votes only. He also shows there from that Mohammad Ali, (original petitioner) filed petition to returning officer promptely on 14.12.97 claiming for recounting of ballot papers immediately on the next day of election held on 13.12.97. He submits that such facts were duly stated by the P.Ws. including the agents (P.W: 2-6) of original petitioner at the final hearing.

7. As regards maintainability of the civil revision under section 115 C.P.C. learned Advocate refers to decisions reported in 9 BLD (1989) page 173 wherein it was held that Election Tribunal is not a civil court under the Civil Courts Act 1887 and it is not a part of the judicial system of the country. The tribunal was created for a limited purpose by a special law and is under the superintendent of the executive authority. Since election tribunal being not a civil court they are not amenable to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division. He refers to the decision reported in 38 DLR page 262 wherein it was similarly held that election tribunal is a creature of statute for some special purpose and not a civil court subordinate to the High Court Division. He contends that the decision re-ported in 38 DLR(AD) page 172 will not hold good as it referred only to District Judge as an election appellate tribunal as per provisions of section 29(4) of Local Government U.P. Ordinance 1983 and not to election tribunal itself. It was held that District Judge mentioned in section 29(4) of the above Ordinance is not a person a designata but a court and as such order of District Judge as election appellate tribunal under section 29(4) will be amenable to revisional jurisdiction of High Court Division under section 115 C.P.C. This case not apply in case of an order passed by election tribunal which is not a civil court and as such in view of decision noticed above the order passed by election tribunal is not amenable to revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 CPC. He therefore contends that the civil revision being against the order of election tribunal cannot be tenable in law as the said order is not amenable to revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 CPC. He finally contends that impugned order has no illegality and error of law occasioning any failure of justice calling for interference by this court. According to him the rule should discharged.

8. On the maintainability of the present civil revision appropriate reference may be made to the decision in the case of Md. Hossain Vs. Md. Sayed Ali and others reported in 9 BLD page 173 where in it was held.

"Election tribunal would have the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of the Civil Procedure only for decision of the matter before it and not beyond. It is not a civil court under the Civil Court s Act 1887 and it is not a part of the judic al system of the country. The tribunal was created for a limited purpose by a special law and it is not a part of the judicial system of the country. The tribunal was created for a limited purpose by a special law and it is under the superintendence of the executive authority. The power of transfer of an election petition is with election commissioner not with the District Judge, the appellate authority which indicates that the election tribunals are not amenable to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure. Since Election tribunals are not civil courts they also are not amenable to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division."

9. In the decision reported in 38 DLR page 262 similar view was taken and held

Election tribunal is a creature of statute for some special purpose and not a civil court subordinate to the High Court Division which has no jurisdiction to entertain an application under section 115 CPC challenging any order passed by Election Tribunal.

10. In the case of Muktad Hossain Mazumder Vs. Abul Basher Mozumder and others reported in 38 DLR page 4 it was held.

"The distinction between the status of an Election Tribunal set up under the Local Government Ordinance 1984 and the District Judge the appellate forum created by section 29(4) of the same Ordinance, is therefore obvious. The Election Tribunal does not function as a part of the judicial system of the country. It is a not civil court. But the District Judge does fiction as a part of the judicial system of the country. It is not a civil court. Therefore an appellate matter that is placed within the jurisdiction of the District Judge as a principal civil court of the original civil jurisdiction whatever be the source of the trial will be governed by the Code of Civil Procedure."

11. In the case of Hosne Zaman Sarker Vs. Election Tribunal (Munshif) and others reported in 38DLR page 435 it was held.

"Election Tribunal is not a civil court constituted under Civil Courts Act 1887. Powers which an election tribunal exercises is a civil court under the Civil Procedure Code while trying an election case does not empower such tribunal to give retrospectives effect. to an amendment effect to an amendment when such amendment has the effect as if a fresh election petition has been filed on the date of amendment."

12. Similar views were taken in the decisions reported in 28DLR page 368. 31DLR page 119, 28DLR page 189 and 27 DLR page 388.

13. In the decision reported in 38DLR (AD) page 172 it was held

"When a District Judge has been defined as the judge of a principal civil court of original jurisdiction by using this expression for constituting the election appellate tribunal and empowering to hear him appeal from decision of an election tribunal it cannot be intended that he is to act as persona designata. Therefore District Judge acting as an election appellate tribunal is not a persona designata but a court subordinate to the High Court Division."

14. Referring to decisions reported in 27 DLR. page 388 and page 373 as cited Honourable Appellate Division observed and held,

"These decisions as would appear from their context, have dealt with election tribunals and not with election appellate authority. No appeal was provided against their decisions. Moreover provisions of the Ordinance which were considered in these cases and led the courts to conclude that from the decision of election tribunal which is not a civil court an application under Article 102 of the Constitution lies. These decisions have therefore no application in the present case."

15. In view of above decisions it has been clear that the election tribunal being not a civil court under the Civil Courts Act 1887 any order passed by the election tribunal cannot be amenable to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Coat Division under section 115 C.P.C. Impugned order dated 10.9.98 being an order passed by the election tribunal cannot be amenable to the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 C.P.C. and as such present civil revision is obviously found to be not at all maintainable.

16. About merit of the rule reliance was placed on the decisions reported in 48DLR(HC) page 560 and 48 DLR(AD)page 59. Both the decisions are on the same case. In both the decisions it was observed and held. that in the absence of any justification. recounting of ballots should not have been  ordered and in the absence of any prayer for doing it immediately after the polling. In both the decisions reference was made to decision reported in 38DLR(AD) page 275.

17. In the case of Md. Sahajahan Vs. Md. Sadeque and others reported in 38DLR(AD) page 275 it was held

"Recounting of ballot papers by the tribunal is not specifically provided in the election rules but it falls within the inherent powers of the tribunal to decide the election dispute. In the instant case the appellant or his representative did not request the presiding officer for recounting the ballot papers. The tribunal found that the election was held and ballot papers were counted in an orderly manner all through and no objection was raised on the spot. before the presiding officer as to the counting of the ballot papers. It was further held and observed, "When recounting would become so necessary depends on the circumstances in each case. In the absence of clear justification no recounting of votes should be directed. Ground work for recounting must be prepared. Recounting should be refused if no prayer for recounting had been made to the presiding officer who is alone empowered to recount on the spot either on his own motion or on request of any candidate."

<u>18. In the present case it was alleged that the mal practice in respect of illegal counting was committed in collusion with the presiding officers of the disputed polling centres on date of election held on 43.12.97. On 14.12.97 the original petitioner Muhammad Ali filed petition to the Returning Officer claiming for re-counting of votes alleging mal practice and unfair and illegal counting of votes by pushing out his agents from the centres. It appears from Annexure A certified copy of original petition in Election Tribunal Case No. 1 of 1988 that original petitioner Md. Ali made clear allegation that his agents were pushed out by the men of opposite party No. 1 Mozammel Haque in collusion with the presiding 'officer of the polling centres and on 14.12.97 he filed petition to returning officer claiming recounting of votes as the difference was by 8 votes only. From the certified copies of deposition of P.Ws. including agents of Mohammad Ali such as P.W.2 Lebu, P.W. 3 Bezu, P.W. 4 A. Latif, P.W.5 A. Samad and P.W.6 Delwar it appears that they all disclosed in deposition that they were pushed out from the polling centre at the time of counting votes. From the impugned order it appears that election tribunal directed recounting in special consideration of the difference between the original petitioner as defeated candidate and elected candidate by only 8 votes. So there was justification of the direction for recounting. Moreover the absence of filing any petition or objection to the presiding officer immediately after the polling by the original petitioner or his agent can not any more stand as a bar or clog in view of latest decision on the point reported in 4 BLC.(AD) page 209 in the case of Kh. Rezaul Karim vs. Md. Babul Hossain another's wherein it was held</u>

<u>"Although no objection regarding counting of invalid votes was raised at the time of counting votes, but omission to raise such objection is no bar to challenge the result of an election in an election petition, as such gives rise to an election dispute which is within the province of the election tribunal to direct recounting of votes."</u>

<u>19. In view of above latest decision on the point reported in 4 BLC(AD) page 209 as above impugned order of election tribunal directing for recounting of votes can not suffer from any legal infirmity and error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning any failure of justice calling for interference by this court, particularly when as per above discussion the civil revision itself appears to be unmaintainable. There is no merit as well in the Rule.</u>

21. In the result the rule is discharged without cost having held the civil revision as unmaintainable. Impugned order dated 10.9.98 stands unaffected. Stay order be re-called. Copy be sent down at once.

End.
