parties:
Shaharbanu and another
Vs.
Lailun Nahar Ershad and others
full_judgment:
Md. Mamtazuddin Ahmed, J: This Rule at the instance of the defendants is directed against the judgment and decree dated 22.2.1998 and 1.3.1998 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 155 of 1995 setting aside those dated 10.4.1995 and 17.4.1995 respectively passed by the Assistant Judge 2nd Additional Court Dhaka in Title Suit No. 143 of 1992 on sent the suit on remand for fresh Trial.

2. The facts for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the suit in the Court of Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka for permanent injunction stating inter alia that the defendant No. 1 is the wife of the defendant No. 2 who entered into agreement with late Sheikh A.M. Ershad predecessor of the plaint for the land and building situated at Municipal Holding No. 3, New Baily Road, under P.S. Ramna, Dhaka at a consideration of Tk. 1,00,000/- and late S.A.M. Ershad paid Tk. 30,000/- to Shahar Banu Mohsin Asghar in presence of her husband with a stipulation to pay the balance at the time of execution and registration of the deed. The defendant No. 1 when delaying the execution and registration of the sale deed on different pleas the predecessor of the plaintiffs late S.A.M. Ershad took possession of the ground floor of the suit property on 3.8.1972 and thereafter he took possession of the entire building and set up office of the Bangladesh Green Cross Society and Bangladesh Advisory Services within the knowledge of the defendants. Late S.A. Ershad made substantial repair and renovation work of the building at a huge cost and also took gas connection paid rents, municipal tax, WASA rates and electricity bills since 1972. Inspite of repeated (sic) to get the sale deed executed and registered but failed and then late Ershad filed Title Suit No. 90 of 1973 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract and the suit was dismissed. On appeal before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court a Division Bench of the said court disallowed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the Trial Court by judgment dated 9.11.1984. And that plaintiffs filed Civil petition for leave to appeal before the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the Trial Court by judgment dated 9.11.1984. And the plaintiffs filed Civil petition for leave to appeal before the Appellate Division and their Lordships accepting the findings of the High Court Division dismissed the Civil Petition No. 113 of 1985 by Judgment dated 8.3.1986.

3. S.M. Ershad died in 1979 leaving being the plaintiffs in possession who filed the suit asserting adverse possession in the suit properties for more than 12 years since 1971 and further stated that the defendant No. 1 asked the plaintiff No. 1 to quit the suit property failing which the defendants would evict the plaintiff forcibly and hence the plaintiffs constrained to file the suit for permanent injunction with the prayer the relevant of which is as

follows:

"To pass a decree for permanent injunction the defendants forms interfering with the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in any manner whatsoever."

4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing joint written statements denying the material allegation made in the plaint stating inter alia that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and nature and the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the entire suit property and the predecessors of the plaintiffs S.A.M. Ershad having

connivance with Mr. Habibur Rahman, Advocate entered into the suit building and land and also created some fraudulent documents. Late S.A.M. Ershad filed a suit for specific performance of contract and the suit was dismissed and the same was affirmed by the High Court Division of the Supreme Court as well as by the Appellate Division and the plaintiff-predecessor, including the plaintiffs being in unlawful and illegal possession can not maintain this suit against the true owner and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. The learned Assistant Judge upon considering the evidences and referring two decisions such as 36 DLR-242 and 10 BLD (DLR) 193 decreed the suit with findings:-

"As the plaintiff side has been able to prove its exclusive possession in the property and as the defendant side could not submit anything as to the Non-maintainability of the suit So, the suit is maintainable in its present from and the plaintiffs are entitled to get relief as prayed by them."

6. The defendants being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree preferred appeal before the District Judge, Dhaka and eventually the appeal was heard by Mr. Md. Mizanur Rahman. Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka who allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, but the suit was sent back on remand for fresh trial in the light of the observation made in the judgment.

7. Mr. Sultan Ahmed with Ms. Tania Ameer, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners, has taken me through the judgments of both the courts below and also the supplementary affidavit to the application and submits that the appellate Court committed no error of law in allowing the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the Trial Court but committed error of law in sending the suit on remand for fresh trial with some observations indicating three issues which on the face of it is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Learned Advocate submits that three issues which have been suggested and directed the Trial Court for holding fresh hearing are no manner appropriate in the facts and circumstances of the case and even if these issues are answered in favour of the plaintiffs and in that case also the suit is not maintainable for permanent injunction because the plaintiffs have no manner of title in the suit properly which had already been found in the suit for specific performance of contract filed by the predecessor of the plaintiffs up to Appellate Division inasmuch as by now the plaintiffs become trespassers in the suit land and building and the trespassers in possession are not entitled to any relief whatsoever, as against true-owner and as such in giving the suit on remand the appellate Court committed fundamental error of law which calls for interference by this Court. Learned Advocate further submits that there are sufficient evidences on record to dispose of the suit no merit and the appellate Court without adverting to the materials on record such as oral and documentary has passed the impugned order though the judicial pronouncement is that the court of Appeal being the last court of facts is require to consider the materials evidences either to after or reverse. But in the present case the appellate court simply shirked its responsibility in sending back the suit on remand to the trial Court without itself deciding the appeal on merit and as such this court is require to decide the suit on merit as sufficient materials both oral and documentary are available on records and this Hon'ble Court is empowered to dispose of the suit on merit being in revisional jurisdiction. To support his contention he has referred to the decision in the case of Hussain Ahmed Chowdhury alias Ahmed Hossain Chowdhury and others vs. Md. Nurul Amin and others reported in 47 DLR(AD)162, wherein their Lordships held.

"It is to be stated here that if there is misreading of evidence and non consideration of some material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional court for consider the same material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional court to consider the same and to arrive at a proper finding on the material evidence on record and to finally dispose of the case. In the instant case even if it is accepted that there is misroading of evidence and non consideration of material evidence then the learned Single Judge was within its competence to dispose of the matter on the materials on record without remanding the suit."

8. Learned Advocate again submits that the suit for permanent injunction and the cause of action is the threat basing upon which the plaintiffs instituted the shit and the plaintiffs valued the suit stating that there is no standard of valuation of the suit of this nature and as such the suit is valued at Tk. 120/- and minimum court fees of Tk. 30/- was paid and such fixation of valuation is not barred by any provision of court fees act and further submits that section 4 and section 8 of the Suits Valuation Act, 1887 and section 7(IV)(d) of the Court-Fees Act, 1870 having not been breached in framing the suit and also making the valuation of the subject matter of the suit inasmuch as the plaintiff has not sought for any declaration of title or confirmation of possession or confirmation of declaration by adverse possession and as the relief sought for is not relating to property and as such no market value has to be assessed or that any separate statement is necessary but the appellate Court only on surmises on those aspect of the Case directed to dispose of the suit though the Trial Court found the suit is maintainable. The learned Advocate further contends that the defendants on appeal also did not take any ground in this respect, the appellate Court having worked on surmises and remanded the suit committed error of law, which calls for interference by this Court as the same has caused failure of justice. Learned Advocate further taking to the judgment of the appellate court at page 4 and 5 submits that the appellate Court was quite unmindful to the facts and circumstances of the case inasmuch as the appellate Court stated that the plaintiff is the appellant and also discussed about the title and possession of the plaintiff having referred to the decisions of High Court Division and the Appellate Division of the Supreme court passed in the earlier suit between the same parties which was the suit for specific performance of contract and stated in the impugned judgment that the appellate Court found that the appellants (it should be respondents) acquired valid title by adverse possession in the suit properties. The portion from the impugned judgment of the Appellate Court (page-5) is quoted for proper appreciation of the contention of the petitioners, which runs thus:

"The decree of dismissal as it was passed by the learned Sub-Judge was upheld up to the Honorable Supreme Court High Court Division as well as in the Appellate Division with the findings that the deed of agreement was invalid one but the plaintiff-respondents continued possession in the suit properties continuously openly and adversely by ascertaining their hostile title against the defendant-appellants and thus acquired valid title by adverse possession in the suit properties."

and the learned Advocate again referring to the judgment of the High Court Division passed in appellate forum arose out of the earlier suit being specific performance of contract which have been annexed with the supplementary affidavit to this revisional application and submits that there was no such findings recorded by their Lordships while disposing the appeal but their Lordships came to the findings in judgment as follows:

"Lastly we find that the plaintiff having by his own act and to have prayed false and made false representation in this suit and exposed his malafides he does not deserve to get the discretionary relief by way of specific performance in his favour."

and again referring to the judgment of the Appellate Division submits that their Lordships while disposing leave petition accepted the findings of the High Court Division and dismissed the Civil petition leave to appeal Nos. 327 and 331 of 1991 the relevant portion of which is quoted which runs this:-

"Findings of the courts below were that the alleged agreement for sale was fraudulent and void. But the strength of that agreement she had forcibly taken possession of the ground floor of the building. These findings were accepted by the Appellate Division in its judgment dated 18 March, 1986, in Civil Petition No. 113 of 1985 which was dismissed.

and submits that a Judicial officer like Additional District Judge has given wrong interpretation to the judgment of the superior courts and he submits that a judge may commit wrong in resolving facts and constructing the documents but in this case the learned judge in giving such wrong findings referring to the decision of the Superior Courts committed misconduct and should be taken into task for making unworthy and wrong statement in the judgment. Learned Advocate again submits that the Trial Court on misquoting the observations from the decision in the case of Chand Mohammad Mondal vs. Rayezuddin Ahmed and others reported in 10 DLR 193 decreed the suit but the observation  so referred to by the Trial Court supports that contention of the defendants but not the plaintiffs to the effect that trespasser cannot get any relief against the person who has got legal title, the relevant portion from the above decision is quoted hereunder.

"In a competition between the plaintiff who is none but a trespasser having no manner of title, I do not think a trespasser should be allowed to avail of the principles of equity by way of injunction as against a person who has got sole legal title to the suit land. Relief of injunction is based on principles of equity and a court of Law or Equity can hardly favour a person who is a trespasser against the person who has got legal title."

9. Learned Advocate then referred to the decision in the case of Md. Gafar and others vs. Azimuddin reported in 36 DLR-242, wherein it has been held:

"In a suit for permanent injunction the plaintiffs are required to prove their exclusive in the suit land and a prima-facie title. In this case it has been clearly found by both the Courts below that the plaintiff and their predecessor have been in exclusive possession of the suit land for over 12 years adversely not he defendants and their predecessor:"

and submits that here in this case, the plaintiff at first claimed possession on the basis of an agreement and filed suit for specific performance of contract and the suit was dismissed up to Appellate Division. The learned Judges of the High Court Division came to the finding's that the claim of the plaintiffs predecessor was found to have made false representation and such findings of the High Court Division is not led us to hold that the possession of the plaintiffs is not adverse as has been found in the decision of the Trial Court but the plaintiffs have to show and prove exclusive possession in the suit property and a prima-facie title but in this case such ingredients are absent and the appellate Court having dismissed the suit committed no error of law but remanding the Same the appellate Court committed error of law.

10. Learned Advocate has referred to few decisions to support his contention to the effect that the trespasser can not claim decree in any form or for permanent injunction against the true owner such as in the case of Sangawwa and others vs. Yemnappa and an-other reported in A.I.R. 1980 Karnataka 220 where in their Lordship held:

"Unless the trial Court has decided the question of the lawful, possession of the plaintiffs on the date of the suit, the suit of the plaintiffs could not be decreed since it was directed against the true owners of the land. In such a situation, the question tenancy is involved for the decision of the Court in a suit for injunction. The question of tenancy shall have to be decided under the provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 after that Act came into force."

Another decision in the case of Khairunnessa being dead her heirs Feroz Alam and others vs. Zobida Nahar alias Zharna and others, reported in 49 DLR(AD)77, it has been held:-

"It baffles understanding how the learned Judges of the High Court Division could justify the ends of justice in passing the order of remand in the face of the glaring Inches and conscious machination of the defendant to procrastinate the litigation herself being in possession of the property which the learned Judges did not fail to notice. Even compensatory costs as awarded in the instant case cannot justify an order of remand in the name of ends of justice when the order itself defeats justice. Ends of justice can never be the caprice or sweet will of a court. The C01111. must proceed on sound principles. Benjamin Cardozo's famous words in the nature of judicial Process, Yale University press, 1921, are apt in this connection which run as follows."

"The judge, even when heirs free, is still not wholly free, he is not to innovate at pleasure. He is not a knight-errant roaming at will in pursuit of his own ideal of beauty or of goodness. He is to draw his inspiration from consecrated principles. He is to yield to spasmodic sentiment to vague and unregulated benevolence. He is to exercise a discretion informed by tradition, methodized by analogy disciplined by system and subordinated to the primordial necessity of order in the social life. Wide enough in all consciences is the field of discretion that remains."

Another decision in the case of Safaruddin and others Vs. Fazlul Huq and others repoKted in 49 DLR(AD)15 1 wherein it has been held:-

"We find no substance in any of the contentions for the following reasons. First the revisional power of the High. Court Division is supervisory power which may also exercised suo-motu. The natural corollary would be that the High Court Division is not obliged to hear the parties before pronouncing its verdict when the parties concerned had opportunities to appear but refrained from doing so."

Another decision in the case of Salam Khatun and others vs. Zilla Parishad Chittagong, represented by its Secretary and another reported in 51 DLR (AD) 257 wherein their Lordships observed that:

"Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, learned Counsel for the plaintiff-petitioners submits that the record of rights have all along been prepared in the name of the plaintiffs predecessors. True, but the plaintiffs could not file any paper to show the alleged Raiyati right of Noor Hossain on the basis of settlement or lease taken from defendant No. 1. The High Court Division was well founded in law in holding that under the circumstances the plaintiffs have established a case of possession but not of title. When they are in possession claiming reiyati settlement they cannot set up adverse possession either. They are not entitled to a declaration of title."

11. Learned Advocate placed a photo copy of the plaint being Title Suit No. 86 of 1998 and submits that in the meantime the defendant-petitioners instituted the suit which is now pending against the defendant-petitioners instituted the suit which is now pending against the defendants for recovery of Khas possession and for manse profits which is also pending for disposal in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka.

<u>12. On examination of the judgment of the appellate Court it has been found that the appellate Court though dismissed the suit but the appellate Court failed to exercise the jurisdiction within the scope of provision of order 41 rule 31 CPC and it is also found that the appellate Court did not properly concentrated to the facts as we well as evidence on record and only on surmises upon setting aside the judgment of the trial Court sent the suit on remand which in any manner cannot be held is a proper judgment rather it is found that the learned Judge without adverting to the materials on record shirked its responsibility in giving, remand the suit to the trial Court which is at all not necessary rather allowing the appeal as it appears committed no error of law. It has further found that the appellate Court failed to find that the suit is not for declaration of title or confirmation of possession upon movable and immovable property rather the suit was filed for permanent injunction under Specific Relief Act alleging that the defendants threatened the plaintiffs and accordingly valued the suit and also paid the court fees and the Trial Court also found that the suit was maintainable but the trial Court in spite of its finding that the plaintiffs acquired no title by adverse possession but on misreading of two decisions such as 36 DLR and 10 DLR/BLD decreed the suit. On the other Appellate Court only on some gauze work and on framing three issues remanded the suit for fresh trial and committed error of law. Which calls for interference by this court. It has been found from the decision reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162 that if this court finds sufficient materials then can dispose of the suit on merit without remanding to the appellate court or to the Trial Court in the appropriate case and having regard to the decision I find sufficient materials on the records to dispose of the suit on merit and in this view of the matter I find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate of the petitioner and as such I am not inclined to send the suit to the appellate Court as well as to the Trial Court on remand and having satisfied on the materials the revisional application before us is disposed of on merit and thereby order of the appellate Court as to sending of the suit on remand is set aside as not being backed by cogent reasons and in this aspect I find the appellate Court committed error of law which calls for interference by this Court. Before parting with the case it is felt incumbent to put on record that the findings arrived at by the appellate Court in appreciating the findings of the High Court Division and Appellate Division which were produced before the appellate Court is found lack of intent and prudence on the part of the appellate Court.</u>

13. In view of my discussions and reasons shown above I am inclined to hold that the appellate Court committed error of law in sending that suit on remand, which caused failure of justice.

14. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The order in remanding the suit to the trial Court passed by the appellate Court is set aside. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is vacated, consequently the suit stands dismissed.

Send down the lower Court records.

End.
